Sam and Mia were twins who liked to go to camp with their mom and dad. They slept in a big tent and played with other kids. They also learned how to make a fire, sing songs and cook food.

One day, they decided to make hot dogs for lunch. They put the meat on sticks and held them over the fire. They also had bread and sauce to put on the meat. Sam liked the red sauce, but Mia liked the yellow sauce.

"Can I try your sauce?" Sam asked Mia.

"Sure, but it is spicy. You might not like it," Mia said.

Sam did not listen. He took some of Mia's sauce and put it on his meat. He took a big bite and then he felt his mouth burn. He coughed and spit out the food. He ran to the water and drank a lot. He felt tears in his eyes.

Mia laughed and said, "I told you it was spicy. You should listen to me. I know what I like and what you like."

Sam was angry and sad. He did not like Mia's sauce or her laugh. He wanted to make her feel bad too. He saw a napkin on the table and had an idea. He wiped his mouth with the napkin and then he wiped his nose too. He made the napkin dirty and wet. He sneaked behind Mia and put the napkin on her head.

Mia felt something on her head and took it off. She saw the napkin and smelled it. She screamed and threw it away. She was disgusted and mad. She looked at Sam and saw him smile. She knew he did it.

"That was mean, Sam. Why did you do that?" Mia asked.

"Because you laughed at me. You hurt my feelings. I wanted to hurt yours," Sam said.

Mom and dad heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. They saw the napkin, the sauce and the kids' faces. They understood what happened and they were not happy.

"Sam, Mia, what did you do?" Mom asked.

They told mom and dad what they did and why they did it. Mom and dad shook their heads and said, "That was not nice. You should not hurt each other. You should love each other. You are twins and you are family. You should share and care and help each other. You should say sorry and hug and make up."

Sam and Mia felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they were wrong and they hurt each other. They said sorry and hugged and made up. They promised to be nice and listen and respect each other. They also promised to be careful with spicy sauce and dirty napkins.

Mom and dad smiled and said, "That's good. We are proud of you. Now, let's have some lunch and enjoy the camp."

They had some lunch and enjoyed the camp. They also learned a lesson: to be kind and loving to each other.

"Mr. Bear, what did you do?" Sam cried. "You ruined your costume. Now you can't be in the show."

"I don't care," the bear said. "I don't want to be in the show. I want to be myself. I don't need a mustache to be smart and handsome."

Sam felt sad and angry too. He loved his bear, but he did not like that he was so stubborn. He did not know what to do. He heard his mom and dad coming upstairs. They wanted to see his show.

"Sam, are you ready?" his mom called.

Sam looked at the bear and the mustache. He had an idea. He smiled and said, "Yes, I am. Come in, please."

He picked up the mustache and put it on his own face. He held the bear in his arms and said, "Welcome to the show. I am Sam, and this is my friend, Mr. Bear. We are going to tell you a story about a mustache."

Mom and dad laughed and clapped. They thought Sam and the bear looked very funny and cute. They sat down and listened to the story. Sam made up a story about how the bear found a mustache in the forest and tried to wear it, but it caused him a lot of trouble. He made the bear talk and act out the story. He made the mustache fall off and stick to different things. He made the bear sneeze and chase the mustache. He made the bear learn a lesson and be happy without the mustache.

The show was a big success. Mom and dad loved it. They praised Sam for his creativity and humor. They hugged him and the bear. They said they were proud of him.

Sam felt happy and proud too. He looked at the bear and said, "I'm sorry, Mr. Bear. I should have listened to you. You were right. You don't need a mustache to be smart and handsome. You are perfect the way you are."

The bear smiled and said, "That's okay, Sam. I'm sorry, too. I should have been more flexible. You were right. The mustache was part of your costume. You were very brave to wear it for the show. You are very smart and handsome, too."

They hugged each other and said, "We are friends."

They put the mustache back in the box and played with the other toys. They had fun and learned to respect each other's feelings. They were happy. The end.

"Can I have the Z, please?" Sara asks Ben.

"No, I want to spin it!" Ben says.

"But I saw it first!" Sara says.

"I don't care, it's mine!" Ben says.

They start to pull the Z from each other. They are both envious of the Z. They do not want to share it. They do not act like friends.

Suddenly, the Z slips from their hands and flies across the room. It hits the window and breaks into two pieces. Sara and Ben are shocked. They look at the broken Z and feel sad. They wish they had not fought over it.

"I'm sorry, Sara," Ben says.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Sara says.

They hug each other and say they are still friends. They pick up the pieces of the Z and try to put them back together. They decide to share the letters and play nicely. They learn that spinning and making words are both fun, but being friends is more important.

Tommy was a bad boy. He liked to steal things from other people. He stole toys, candy, books and even money. He did not care if they were sad or angry. He only wanted to have more things for himself.

One night, he saw a big house with many lights and decorations. He thought there must be many nice things inside. He sneaked into the garden and looked for a way to get in. He saw a chimney on the roof. He thought he could climb up and go down the chimney.

He climbed up a tree and jumped onto the roof. He walked to the chimney and looked inside. It was dark and dirty. He did not like it, but he wanted to see what was in the house. He put his feet in the chimney and started to slide down.

But he did not know that someone was waiting for him. It was Santa Claus. He had come to bring presents to the good children in the house. He heard Tommy coming down the chimney and he was very angry. He grabbed Tommy by the legs and pulled him out.

Tommy was scared and surprised. He saw Santa Claus's face and beard. He saw his red suit and his big bag of presents. He saw his attractive smile and his twinkling eyes. He felt ashamed and sorry. He knew he had been very naughty.

Santa Claus looked at Tommy and shook his head. He said, "Tommy, you have been a very bad boy. You have stolen many things from other people. You have made them unhappy and hurt. You have been selfish and greedy. You have not been good at all."

Tommy felt tears in his eyes. He said, "I'm sorry, Santa. I know I have been bad. I don't know why I do it. I don't need all these things. I just want to be happy and have friends. But no one likes me. They say I'm a thief and a liar. They don't want to play with me."

Santa Claus sighed and said, "Tommy, stealing is not the way to be happy or have friends. Stealing is wrong and bad. It makes you and others unhappy and lonely. You need to learn to be good and kind. You need to share and care. You need to say sorry and give back what you have stolen. You need to make amends and be honest. Then you will be happy and have friends. Then you will be good and deserve presents."

Tommy nodded and said, "I understand, Santa. I want to be good and kind. I want to share and care. I want to say sorry and give back what I have stolen. I want to make amends and be honest. I want to be happy and have friends. I want to be good and deserve presents. Can you help me, Santa?"

Santa Claus smiled and said, "Of course, Tommy. I will help you. But you have to help yourself too. You have to try hard and change your ways. You have to listen and learn. You have to be brave and humble. You have to be respectful and grateful. You have to be loving and generous. You have to be the best you can be. Then you will be a good boy and a good friend. Then you will have a good life and a good Christmas."

Tommy smiled and said, "Thank you, Santa. I will try hard and change my ways. I will listen and learn. I will be brave and humble. I will be respectful and grateful. I will be loving and generous. I will be the best I can be. I will be a good boy and a good friend. I will have a good life and a good Christmas."

Santa Claus hugged Tommy and said, "You're welcome, Tommy. I'm proud of you. I'm glad you have learned your lesson. I'm happy you have a good heart. I'm hopeful you have a bright future. I'm here to help you and support you. I'm your friend and your Santa."

Tommy hugged Santa and said, "I love you, Santa. You're the best. You're my friend and my Santa."

Santa Claus put Tommy in his sleigh and said, "Let's go, Tommy. Let's return what you have stolen and say sorry to the people you have hurt. Let's spread some joy and peace. Let's make this a merry Christmas for everyone."

Tommy said, "Let's go, Santa. Let's do it. Let's make this a merry Christmas for everyone."

And they flew away in the sky, with the reindeer and the bells, with the stars and the moon, with the presents and the smiles, with the love and the hope, with the magic and the wonder, with the spirit and the meaning, of Christmas.

"Let me try," Lily said. She took the stick from Ben and hit the lock too. But it did not open either. She hit it harder and harder, but it still did not open.

The wave crashed on the shore and swept them and the box into the sea. They screamed and tried to swim, but the water was too strong and too deep. They sank with the box and never came back.

The moral of the story is: Do not be greedy and curious about things that are not yours. Pay attention to your surroundings and listen to warnings. The harbor can be a dangerous place.

Sara liked to eat candy. She ate candy every day. She did not like to eat other food. She did not like to eat celery. Celery was green and crunchy and had no sugar.

One day, Sara's mom said, "Sara, you have to eat some celery. It is good for you. It will make you strong and healthy. If you eat some celery, I will give you a candy later."

Sara did not want to eat celery. But she wanted candy. She said, "OK, mom. I will eat some celery. But you have to promise to give me candy later."

Sara's mom said, "I promise, Sara. But you have to eat all the celery on your plate. It is not much. It is easy to eat."

Sara took a bite of celery. She did not like it. It was bitter and hard. She made a face. She wanted to spit it out. But she remembered the candy. She swallowed the celery. She took another bite. And another. And another. She ate all the celery on her plate.

Sara's mom said, "Good job, Sara. You ate all the celery. I am proud of you. You kept your promise. Now you can have a candy."

Sara's mom gave Sara a candy. Sara was happy. She ate the candy. It was sweet and soft. She liked it. But she noticed something. The candy did not taste as good as before. It tasted too sweet. It made her thirsty. She wanted some water.

Sara's mom said, "Sara, do you like the candy?"

Sara said, "Yes, mom. But not as much as before. The candy is too sweet. I like the water better. And you know what, mom? The celery was not so bad. It was crunchy and fresh. It made me feel good. Can I have some more celery tomorrow?"

Sara's mom said, "Of course, Sara. You can have some more celery tomorrow. And maybe some other food too. There are many good foods to try. You just have to be brave and try them. You might like them. And you will be strong and healthy."

Sara said, "OK, mom. I will try other food too. But can I still have some candy sometimes?"

Sara's mom said, "Yes, Sara. You can still have some candy sometimes. But not too much. And only after you eat some good food. That is the deal."

Sara said, "OK, mom. That is the deal. I promise."

The moral of the story is: You should eat a variety of food, not just candy. You should keep your promises. You should be brave and try new things. You might like them.

Tom hears a scream and turns around. He sees Ben holding the axe and blood dripping from his finger. He drops his axe and runs to Ben. He is scared and angry. He takes the axe from Ben and puts it back in the shed. He wraps Ben's finger with a cloth and hugs him.

He says, "Ben, you should never touch the axe. It is not a toy. It can hurt you very badly. You are lucky that you only cut your finger. Next time, you could lose your hand or your arm. You have to listen to me and stay away from the axe. Do you understand?"

Ben nods and says, "I'm sorry, dad. I won't touch the axe again. I love you."

Tom says, "I love you too, Ben. But you have to be careful and smart. The axe is for chopping wood, not for playing. Come on, let's go inside and clean your wound. And don't worry, your finger will heal soon."

The rope and the knot became friends and the rope always helped by stretching when the knot was in a tight spot.

The big dog and the little cat went to the tree and found their ball. They were so happy. They thanked the bird and the squirrel. From that day on, they always united when they had trouble. And they were never upset again.

The food friends kept on quarreling. They did not stop. Then, the big cook came into the kitchen. The cook saw the quarrel and decided to make a big soup. His friends helped him by putting the basketball in a basket and using it to distract the dog. The dog chased after the basketball and Timmy and his friends were able to run away. From then on, Timmy always brought his modest basketball to the park and played with his friends without fear.

As the top spun, Tom started to spin too. He spun around in his red cape, just like the top. They spun and spun, having so much fun. Tom and the top were very happy, and they played together all day long.

Then, Sam's friend, a dog named Max, came to help. Max grabbed the cord in his mouth and pulled it off the chair. Sam was so happy! Now, he could sit on his soft chair without the cord. Sam and Max played together and had a fun day.

Tim and Bob started to run as fast as they could. They raced through the grass, laughing and having fun. Tim shouted, "I am going to win, Bob!" Bob replied, "No, I am faster!"

As they neared the finish line, Tim's hook caught on a tree branch. It slowed him down, but it also made a big swing. Tim swung forward and crossed the finish line first. Tim and Bob laughed and hugged each other. They were both winners because they had so much fun racing together.

She put the pastry in the oven and waited. She smelled the sweet aroma and smiled. She took out the pastry and put it on a plate. It looked delicious. She was about to take a bite when she heard a knock on the door.

She opened the door and saw a boy with curly hair and a big smile. He was holding a basket of flowers. He said, "Hello, I'm Tom. I live next door. I saw you baking and I wanted to give you these flowers. They are for you."

Lila was surprised and shy. She said, "Thank you, Tom. That's very kind of you. Do you want to come in? I have a pastry to share."

"Look, a bee!" Tim said. "It is yellow and black and has wings."

"Be careful, Tim," Lily said. "Bees can sting. It hurts a lot. I am anxious of bees."

Tim was not afraid. He wanted to touch the bee. He reached out his hand slowly. The bee did not like that. It buzzed louder and flew away.

"Come back, bee!" Tim shouted. "I want to play with you!"

Lily shook her head. She thought Tim was silly. She did not want to play with bees. She wanted to play with something else.

"Let's go, Tim," she said. "We can play with the ball or the dolls or the blocks. They are more fun than bees."

Tim was sad. He liked bees. He thought they were pretty and interesting. He did not understand why Lily was anxious of them. He followed her to the other side of the garden. He hoped to see the bee again. Maybe it would come back and play with him.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play with boats. They had a big boat with a blue anchor that they could pull up and down. One day, they decided to go to the lake and sail their boat. They put on their life jackets and got on the boat.

But soon, they had a problem. Tim wanted to go to the left side of the lake, where there were ducks and fish. Sam wanted to go to the right side of the lake, where there were rocks and frogs. They both pulled the steering wheel in different directions, and the boat started to shake and spin.

"Stop it, Tim!" Sam shouted. "I want to go to the rocks!"

"No, Sam!" Tim yelled back. "I want to go to the ducks!"

They did not listen to each other, and they did not share. They kept pulling and pushing, and the boat went faster and faster. The anchor swung in the air, and hit the side of the boat. It made a loud noise and a big hole.

The water started to come in the boat, and the boat started to sink. Tim and Sam were scared and wet. They tried to grab the anchor, but it was too heavy and too late. The boat went under the water, and they had to swim to the shore.

They were very sad and sorry. They had lost their boat and their anchor. They had also lost their friendship. They had not been honest and kind to each other. They had been selfish and mean. They had learned a hard lesson. They wished they had not separated.

"Look, Mom, look!" Ben shouted, pointing to the sky. "A big bird!"

Mom looked up and saw a large, white bird with a long neck and a yellow beak. "That's a swan, Ben. It's a very beautiful bird. It came from far away, from the east, where the sun rises."

"Can we feed it, Mom?" Mia asked, holding a piece of bread in her hand.

"Sure, we can. But be careful, it might bite. Swans can be very strong and fierce. Let's go closer, but slowly and quietly."

Mom, Ben and Mia walked towards the pond, where the swan was swimming. The swan saw them and swam closer, too. It stretched its neck and opened its beak.

"Hello, swan," Ben said softly. "We have some bread for you. Do you want some?"

The swan nodded and took a bite of the bread from Ben's hand. It tasted good. The swan made a soft sound, like a whistle.

"Wow, it likes it!" Mia said, smiling. She gave another piece of bread to the swan. The swan ate it and whistled again.

Mom took a picture of Ben, Mia and the swan with her phone. She was happy to see them having fun. She said, "What a nice day! We made a new friend. Maybe we'll see the swan again next time we come to the park."

But the big star is not a star. It is a button. It belongs to Mom's new coat. Mom does not know that Ben and Jen took it. She is looking for it.

Ben and Jen do not know that the button is a button. They think it is a star. They put it in the middle of their picture. They say, "Look, our picture is so pretty. The big star is the best. It is so smart. It shines more than the other stars."

But then, something happens. The button is not a smart star. It is a silly button. It makes a loud noise. It says, "Beep, beep, beep!" Ben and Jen are scared. They do not like the noise. They run to Mom.

Mom hears the noise. She sees the button. She sees the picture. She says, "Oh, no! That is not a star. That is my button. You took it from my coat. That is not good. You have to give it back."

Ben and Jen are sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not know. We thought it was a star. It was so shiny. We wanted to play with it."

Mom is not angry. She is glad. She says, "It is okay. I understand. You like stars. But you have to ask before you take something. And you have to be careful. Some things are not what they seem. They can be dangerous or noisy or break."

Ben and Jen nod. They say, "We will ask. We will be careful. We will not take things that are not ours."

Mom hugs them. She says, "I love you. You are my stars. You are smart and shiny and good."

Ben and Jen smile. They say, "We love you, Mom. You are our star. You are smart and shiny and good, too."

They start to argue. Tom says, "It is my turn to open it!" Lily says, "No, it is mine! You had it first!" They tug and tug on the zipper, but it only makes it worse.

Their mom comes to the closet. She sees them fighting over the bag. She says, "What are you doing? You need to eat. And you need to share. Fighting will not help you open the bag. It will only break the zipper."

She takes the bag from them. She shows them how to improve the zipper. She says, "You need to be gentle and patient. You need to move the zipper slowly and carefully. Like this." She slides the zipper back and forth until it is smooth.

She opens the bag. She says, "Look, there are some clothes and toys for you. They are from your grandma. She sent them for your birthday. Aren't they nice?"

Tom and Lily are happy. They say, "Thank you, mom. Thank you, grandma." They hug their mom and each other. They say, "We are sorry for fighting. We will share the clothes and toys. And we will improve our zipper skills."

They go to the kitchen. They eat their lunch. They are not hungry anymore. They are glad they learned how to improve the zipper. And they are glad they have each other.

"Look, Max, a cactus!" she said.

"No, Lily, don't touch it! It will hurt you!" Max said.

But Lily did not listen. She reached out her hand and touched the cactus. Ouch! She felt a pain in her finger. She started to cry.

"Mommy, mommy, it hurts!" she cried.

Mommy came running. She saw Lily's finger. She saw the cactus.

"Oh, Lily, you touched the cactus. That was not a good idea. The cactus has needles that can poke you. Come, let me cover your finger with a band-aid," she said.

She took Lily inside the house. She washed her finger and put a band-aid on it. The band-aid was pink with a heart on it.

"There, there, Lily, it will be better soon. Next time, be careful with the cactus, okay?" she said.

"Okay, mommy, I'm sorry. I like the pink band-aid. Thank you, mommy," Lily said.

She hugged mommy and smiled. Max came inside too. He gave Lily a hug and said he was sorry too.

They decided to play with their toys instead of the cactus. They learned their lesson. The cactus was not a toy. It was a plant that needed to be left alone.

Lila and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park and look for shiny things. One day, they found a big shiny thing under a tree. It was a trophy. It had a star on top and a name on the bottom. The name was very old and hard to read.

"Wow, look at this!" Lila said. "It's so shiny and pretty. I wonder who it belongs to."

"Maybe it's a magic trophy," Ben said. "Maybe it can make wishes come true. Let's try it."

They rubbed the trophy and closed their eyes. They wished for candy and toys and fun.

But nothing happened. The trophy did not make any sound or light. It just stayed shiny and still.

"Maybe it's broken," Lila said. "Maybe it's too old to work."

"Or maybe it's a bad trophy," Ben said. "Maybe it's a trap. Maybe someone left it here to trick us."

They heard a loud roar behind them. They turned around and saw a big angry bear. The bear had smelled the trophy and wanted it. It had followed them to the park. It was hungry and mad.

"Run!" Lila screamed. "It's a bear!"

Suddenly, the match lit up. It made a bright light and a loud sound. Tom and Lily were scared. They dropped the matches and ran away. The matches fell on the grass and started a fire. The fire grew bigger and bigger. It made smoke and heat.

"Who did this?" one of them asked. He was angry and stern.

Tom and Lily were hiding behind a tree. They felt guilty and ashamed. They knew they had done something bad. They came out and said, "We did. We're sorry. We didn't know."

The firefighter shook his head and said, "You should never play with matches. They are not toys. They are dangerous. They can hurt you and others. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, we understand. We won't do it again. We're sorry."

Tom and Lily agreed and said, "Yes, we will. Thank you."

They hugged each other and went home. They learned a lesson that day. They never played with matches again. They only played with safe and fun things. They were still friends who liked to play in the park. But they were also smarter and wiser.

They took two cups and poured some juice into them. But the juice was too sour. They made faces and spat it out.

"Yuck! This juice is bad!" Lily said.

"Maybe we need to mix it with something," Ben said.

He looked around and saw a bowl of sugar. He took a spoon and scooped some sugar into his cup. He stirred it with the spoon.

"Try this," he said to Lily. "It will make the juice sweet."

Lily took a sip of Ben's juice. It was very sweet. She liked it.

"Mmm, this is good!" she said.

She took some sugar and put it in her cup too. She mixed it with the juice.

They drank their sweet juice and smiled.

But they did not know that the juice was not juice. It was vinegar. Their mom had put it on the table to make a salad. She was in the kitchen, chopping some vegetables. She was ignorant of what Lily and Ben were doing.

When she came back to the table, she saw the empty bottle of vinegar and the cups with sugar. She was shocked.

"What have you done?" she asked Lily and Ben.

They looked at her and said, "We drank some juice. It was sour, so we mixed it with sugar. It was good."

Their mom shook her head and said, "That was not juice. That was vinegar. It is not good for you to drink it. It can make you sick. And you wasted a lot of sugar. That was very naughty of you."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They did not know that they had done something wrong. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We were thirsty. We wanted some juice."

Their mom sighed and said, "It's OK. I forgive you. But next time, ask me before you take something from the table. And don't mix things that don't belong together. Come, I will give you some real juice. And some water to wash away the vinegar."

She took them to the kitchen and gave them some juice and water. They drank them and felt better.

They learned their lesson. They never mixed vinegar and sugar again.

She was happy with what she had.

The fireman gave him a sticker with a fireman and a truck on it. He stuck it on his hat. He was very happy.

"Can I ask you something?" Tommy said. He noticed something on the fireman's arm. It was a bandage. "Are you hurt?"

The fireman looked at his arm. He remembered the fire he fought yesterday. He got a burn from a hot wire. It hurt a lot. But he was brave and did his job.

"A little bit," the fireman said. "But it's okay. It will heal soon. It's part of being a fireman. Sometimes you get hurt, but you always help others."

Tommy nodded. He understood. He wanted to be like the fireman. He wanted to help others too.

"You're very brave," Tommy said. He hugged the fireman. "You're my hero."

The fireman hugged him back. He felt proud and happy. He liked Tommy. He was a good kid.

"You're my hero too, Tommy," the fireman said. "You're a great fireman. Keep playing and dreaming. Maybe one day, you'll be a real fireman."

Tommy smiled. He thanked the fireman and said goodbye. He ran back to his house. He played with his fireman toy. He put out fires and saved people. He wore his hat and his sticker. He made siren noises with his mouth. He was a happy fireman.

Tom and Sue went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. Tom found a big shell that was shiny and pink. He showed it to Sue and said, "Look, Sue, I found a big shell. It is pretty."

Sue wanted to see the shell too. She asked Tom, "Can I hold it, Tom? Please?" Tom said, "OK, but be careful. It is my shell." He gave the shell to Sue and watched her.

Sue held the shell in her hands and looked at it. She saw a hole in the shell and wondered what was inside. She put her ear to the hole and listened. She heard a funny noise, like a snore. She said, "Tom, there is something in the shell. It is making a noise."

Tom said, "What? Let me hear." He took the shell from Sue and put his ear to the hole. He heard the noise too. He said, "It sounds like a crab. Maybe it is sleeping in the shell."

Sue said, "Can we wake it up, Tom? I want to see the crab." Tom said, "OK, let's try. Maybe if we squeeze the shell, it will come out." He squeezed the shell with his fingers and waited.

Suddenly, the shell snapped open and a big crab jumped out. It was angry and scared. It pinched Tom's finger with its claw and made him cry. It ran away to the water and hid under a rock. Tom dropped the shell and said, "Ow, ow, ow! That hurt! Bad crab, bad crab!"

Sue felt sorry for Tom and hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't know the crab would do that. Are you OK?" Tom said, "It's OK, Sue. I'm fine. But I don't like that shell anymore. It is not pretty. It is mean."

Mom and Dad heard Tom cry and came to see what happened. They saw the shell and the crab and understood. They said, "Oh, Tom and Sue, you found a big shell with a crab inside. That was a surprise. But you have to be careful with shells. Some of them have animals that don't like to be disturbed. They can bite or pinch you. Next time, ask us before you touch a shell. We can help you find out what is inside."

Tom and Sue said, "OK, Mom and Dad. We're sorry. We won't touch shells without asking you. We learned our lesson." They kissed Mom and Dad and said, "We love you." Mom and Dad said, "We love you too." They smiled and hugged Tom and Sue and took them to find some ice cream. They had a good day at the beach.

"I did not destroy your drum. It was Tim. He hit the drum too hard. He did not listen to me. I lied to protect him. He is my friend."

The boy replied, "I don't like to brush my hair. It's boring." 

Lily said, "But if you don't brush your hair, it will look ugly. You should take care of it like I do." 

The boy thought about it and decided to start brushing his hair. From that day on, his hair looked neat and tidy, just like Lily's. They played together happily ever after. The end.

Lily searched high and low, but she couldn't find Jack anywhere. She was starting to get worried when suddenly she heard a giggle coming from behind a tree. Jack had hidden himself behind the tree all along!

Lily was happy that Jack kept his promise, but she also thought it was a little selfish of him to hide so well that she couldn't find him. She told Jack how she felt and he apologized. From then on, they promised to play fair and not be selfish when they played games together.

Lily groaned and said, "But Mommy, I don't like cleaning. It's boring."

Lily's eyes widened with excitement. "Can I help weigh him?" she asked.

After they finished weighing the teddy bear, Lily helped her mom dust her room. It wasn't as boring as she thought it would be, and she felt proud of herself for helping out.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy ship in the bathtub. They liked to make the ship sail and splash in the water. They pretended they were pirates and sailors.

"Ahoy, matey!" Ben said. "Let's find some treasure!"

"Okay!" Lily said. "But watch out for the sharks!"

They made the ship go around the tub, looking for shiny things. They found a soap bar, a rubber duck, and a hair clip. They put them on the ship and said they were gold, diamonds, and pearls.

They were having so much fun that they did not hear their mom calling them.

"Lily! Ben! Time to get out and wash up!" Mom said.

But Lily and Ben did not listen. They kept playing with their ship and their treasure. They were being naughty.

Mom came into the bathroom and saw the mess. There was water everywhere. The ship was sinking. The treasure was floating. Mom was not happy.

"Lily! Ben! What are you doing?" Mom said. "You did not listen to me. You did not wash up. You made a big mess. You are naughty!"

Lily and Ben looked at Mom. They felt sorry. They knew they did something bad.

"We are sorry, Mom," they said. "We were just playing. We like our ship. We like our treasure."

Mom sighed. She loved her children, but they needed to learn.

"I know you like your ship and your treasure, but you also need to follow the rules," Mom said. "You need to listen to me. You need to wash up. You need to be good. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They understood. They wanted to be good.

"Yes, Mom," they said. "We understand. We will wash up. We will be good."

Mom smiled. She hugged them and kissed them. She helped them wash up and dry off. She put their ship and their treasure away.

"Maybe tomorrow you can play with your ship and your treasure again, but only if you are good," Mom said.

Lily and Ben smiled. They agreed. They loved their ship and their treasure, but they loved their mom more. They said good night and went to bed. They dreamed of sailing and splashing in the bathtub.

Lily loved her hairy sweater. It was pink and soft and warm. She wore it every day, even when it was hot. She did not want to take it off.

One day, Mom said, "Lily, your sweater is dirty. You need to wash it."

Lily shook her head. "No, Mom, I don't want to wash it. It will lose its hair."

Mom said, "Don't worry, Lily, it will not lose its hair. It will be clean and fluffy. Come on, let's wash it together."

Lily did not like this idea. She hugged her sweater tight. She said, "No, Mom, please, no. I love my sweater. It is mine."

Mom said, "Lily, I know you love your sweater, but it is not good to wear a dirty sweater. It can make you sick. And it smells bad. Please, Lily, let me wash it. I will be gentle. I will use cold water and soft soap. And I will dry it in the sun. It will be as good as new."

Lily looked at Mom. She saw that Mom was not angry. She was kind. She wanted to help Lily. Lily felt a little bit sorry. She said, "Okay, Mom, you can wash it. But only for a little while. And you have to give it back to me."

Mom smiled. She said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good girl. I will wash it and give it back to you. I promise."

Mom took the sweater and put it in a bucket. She poured some water and soap. She rubbed the sweater gently. Lily watched. She felt nervous. She hoped her sweater would be okay.

After a few minutes, Mom rinsed the sweater and wrung it out. She said, "Look, Lily, your sweater is clean. It is still hairy. See?"

Lily came closer. She touched the sweater. It was wet and cold. But it was also clean and hairy. She said, "Yes, Mom, it is still hairy. And it is clean. It does not smell bad."

Mom said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily. Now let's hang it on the line. It will dry soon. Then you can wear it again."

Lily nodded. She helped Mom hang the sweater on the line. She said, "Thank you, Mom, for washing my sweater. You are a good mom."

Mom hugged Lily. She said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love you. And I love your sweater too."

Tim and Kim were friends who liked to make things with paper and glue. They had many colors of paper and a big bottle of glue. One day, they wanted to make a paper snake. They cut long strips of paper and glued them together. They made a long and colorful snake.

"Look at our snake!" Tim said. "It is so pretty and long. We are very good at making things."

"Yes, we are," Kim said. "But I want to make it more fun. Let's twist it and make it look like it is moving."

Kim grabbed one end of the snake and Tim grabbed the other. They started to twist the snake, but they twisted too hard. The glue was not dry yet, and the paper started to tear. The snake broke into many pieces.

"Oh no!" Tim said. "We ruined our snake. It is not pretty and long anymore. It is ugly and short."

Kim started to cry. "I'm sorry, Tim. It was my fault. I wanted to twist it too much. I was not humble. I was proud and silly."

Tim was angry and sad. He did not want to be friends with Kim anymore. He threw the pieces of the snake at Kim and ran away. Kim was left alone with the broken snake and the glue. She wished she had been more humble and careful. She had lost her friend and her snake.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with their toys and watch the birds. One day, Lily has a new toy. It is a camera. She can take pictures of anything she sees.

"Look, Ben, I have a camera!" Lily says. "I can send you pictures of my view!"

"Wow, that is cool!" Ben says. "Can I see?"

Lily shows Ben how to use the camera. She presses a button and the camera makes a sound. Then she shows Ben the picture on the screen.

"Look, I took a picture of the tree!" Lily says.

"That is a nice tree!" Ben says.

Lily and Ben take turns with the camera. They take pictures of the flowers, the sky, the dog, and each other. They have fun.

But then, Lily makes a mistake. She presses the wrong button. The camera sends all the pictures to her mom's phone.

"Oh no!" Lily says. "I did not want to do that!"

Lily's mom sees the pictures on her phone. She smiles. She thinks they are cute. But she also sees one picture that makes her laugh. It is a picture of Lily with a funny face. She has her tongue out and her eyes crossed.

Lily's mom sends the picture back to Lily. She writes: "You are so silly, Lily!"

Lily sees the picture on the camera. She feels embarrassed. She does not like her funny face.

"Mom, why did you send that?" Lily says.

Ben sees the picture too. He thinks it is funny. He laughs.

"Ha ha, Lily, you look funny!" Ben says.

Lily does not like that. She feels more embarrassed. She hides the camera.

"Stop laughing, Ben!" Lily says.

Ben stops laughing. He sees that Lily is upset. He wants to make her feel better.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben says. "You don't look funny. You look nice. You are my friend."

Lily feels a little better. She smiles.

"Thank you, Ben," Lily says. "You are my friend too."

Lily and Ben hug. They are still friends. They play with the camera again. But they are careful not to press the wrong button.

Anna likes to play in the garden. She likes to look for bugs and flowers and rocks. One day, she sees something red and shiny under a big leaf. She moves the leaf and finds an apple.

Anna is happy. She loves apples. They are sweet and juicy and good for her. She picks up the apple and wipes it on her dress. She wants to eat it right away. But then she hears her mom calling her.

"Anna, it's time for lunch! Come inside, please!"

Anna does not want to leave her apple. She wants to save it for later. She looks around the garden and sees a hole in the fence. She runs to the hole and puts the apple inside. She thinks it is a good hiding place. No one will find it there.

She runs back to her mom and goes inside. She eats her lunch and drinks her milk. She tells her mom about the apple she found. Her mom smiles and says she can have it after her nap.

Anna is excited. She can't wait to eat her apple. She goes to her bed and falls asleep. She dreams of the red and shiny apple.

They went to get some tape and glue and stickers and fixed their cars. Then they played with them again, but this time they did not race. They just had fun and shared their cars. They were happy and proud.

Anna and Ben were having lunch with their mom. Mom made soup for them, because it was cold outside. Anna liked soup, but Ben did not. He wanted pizza.

"Mom, can I have pizza instead of soup?" Ben asked.

"No, Ben, you have to eat your soup. It is good for you and it will keep you warm," Mom said.

"But I don't like soup. It is too hot and too wet," Ben said. He made a face and pushed his bowl away.

Anna saw Ben's bowl and had an idea. She wanted more soup, because she was still hungry. She reached for Ben's bowl, but she was clumsy. She knocked over her own bowl and spilled soup all over the table.

"Oh no, Anna, what have you done?" Mom said. She got up and grabbed a cloth to clean the mess.

"I'm sorry, Mom, I was trying to get Ben's soup. He doesn't want it," Anna said.

"Well, that was not a good way to do it, Anna. You have to ask first, and be careful with your bowl. Now we have to leave the table and change your clothes. You are all wet and sticky," Mom said.

Anna felt bad. She did not mean to make a mess. She looked at Ben and hoped he was not mad at her.

"Ben, I'm sorry, I wanted your soup," Anna said.

Ben looked at Anna and smiled. He was not mad at her. He knew she was clumsy, but she was also nice.

"It's okay, Anna, I don't mind. You can have my soup next time. But maybe you should use a spoon," Ben said.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big sack full of dolls and cars and blocks. Ben had a small cord that he liked to tie around things. Lily was very bossy and did not like to share her toys. She said to Ben, "This is my sack and these are my toys. You can't touch them. Go play with your cord somewhere else."

Ben felt sad and angry. He wanted to play with some of the toys in the sack, but Lily would not let him. He thought of a way to get back at her. He waited until Lily was not looking and then he used his cord to tie the sack shut. He made a big knot that was hard to undo. Then he ran away and hid behind the sofa.

Lily did not notice what Ben had done until she wanted to change her doll's dress. She reached for the sack and tried to open it, but it was stuck. She pulled and tugged, but the cord was too tight. She started to cry and yell, "Help! Help! My sack is broken! I can't get my toys out!"

Ben heard Lily's cries and felt sorry for her. He realized that he had been mean and that he should not have tied the sack. He came out from behind the sofa and said to Lily, "I'm sorry, Lily. I tied the sack because you were bossy and did not share your toys. But that was wrong of me. I will help you untie the cord."

Lily stopped crying and looked at Ben. She said, "I'm sorry, too, Ben. I was bossy and did not share my toys. But that was wrong of me. I will let you play with some of my toys if you want."

Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. That is very nice of you. I will share my cord with you if you want."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Ben. That is very nice of you. I will share my dolls and cars and blocks with you if you want."

They hugged and said, "We are sorry. We are friends."

They worked together to untie the cord and opened the sack. They shared their toys and played happily in the living room.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Being bossy is not nice. Saying sorry is good.

Mark threw the banana in the trash. He tried to clean the car, but the mark was still there. He was sad. He had ruined his favorite toy.

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tap near the pond. The tap is shiny and attractive. Lila and Tom want to touch it.

"Can we touch the tap?" Lila asks Tom.

"I don't know. Maybe it is not for us." Tom says.

But Lila is curious. She runs to the tap and turns it. Water comes out of the tap. It is cold and wet. Lila laughs and splashes Tom.

Tom is scared too. He tries to turn the tap again. But it is stuck. He cannot move it.

"Help! Help!" Lila and Tom shout. They hope someone will hear them.

A man hears them. He is the park keeper. He comes to the tap. He sees the water and the puddle. He sees Lila and Tom. He is angry.

"What are you doing here? This tap is not for playing. It is for the pond. You broke it. Now the pond will end. The fish and the ducks will have no water." He says.

Lila and Tom are sorry. They did not mean to break the tap. They did not know it was for the pond. They say sorry to the man.

The man is still angry. But he is also kind. He knows they are just children. He calls a plumber. The plumber comes and fixes the tap. The water stops. The pond is safe.

Lila and Tom are happy. They thank the man and the plumber. They promise to never touch the tap again. They go back to their parents. They tell them what happened. Their parents are not happy. But they are also glad. They hug Lila and Tom. They say they love them.

One day, a new boy came to their street. His name was Sam. He saw Tom and Lily playing music. He wanted to join them. He asked, "Can I play music with you?"

Tom and Lily looked at him. They did not know him. They did not want to share their drum and flute. They said, "No, you can't. These are our toys. You have to find your own."

Sam felt sad. He walked away. He looked for something to play music with. He found a tin can and a stick. He banged the can with the stick. He made a different sound. He liked it.

Tom and Lily heard Sam's sound. They did not like it. They thought it was noisy and bad. They said, "Stop that! You are ruining our music. Go away!"

Sam did not stop. He kept banging the can. He said, "I like my music. It is fun. You are mean. You don't want to share."

Tom and Lily got angry. They shouted at Sam. They told him to be quiet. They did not want to hear his music.

A lady came out of her house. She heard the noise. She saw Tom, Lily and Sam. She asked, "What is going on here? Why are you making so much noise?"

Tom and Lily said, "We are playing music. But he is making a bad sound. He is bothering us. He has to go away."

Sam said, "I am playing music too. But they are not nice. They don't want to share. They have to let me play."

The lady said, "Music is a good thing. It can make people happy and friendly. But you have to respect each other. You have to listen to each other. You have to share and take turns. That is how you make good music together."

Tom and Lily thought about what the lady said. They felt sorry. They realized they were not nice to Sam. They said, "We are sorry, Sam. We were not fair. You can play music with us. You can use our drum and flute. We can use your can and stick. We can try different sounds."

Sam smiled. He said, "Thank you, Tom and Lily. I am sorry, too. I was not polite. You can play music with me. You can use my can and stick. I can use your drum and flute. We can have fun together."

The lady said, "That is very good. I am proud of you. You are learning to be kind and friendly. You are making good music together."

Tom, Lily and Sam played music together. They shared and took turns. They listened and learned. They made loud and happy sounds. They had fun. They became friends.

When Lily got to the party, she saw that there were lots of big kids there. They were playing rough games and didn't want to play with her. Lily felt scared and alone.

She wanted to go home, but she didn't know how. She started to cry and her mom had to come and pick her up. Lily learned that sometimes things may not be safe or fun, even if we really want them to be.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little birdie. He lived in a nest high up in a tree. One day, a big wind came and scatter all the birdie's nest on the ground.

"Oh no! My nest!" cried the birdie.

A little girl heard the birdie's cry and woke up from her nap. She saw the poor birdie on the ground and said, "Don't worry little birdie, I'll help you make a new nest."

The little girl gathered some sticks and leaves and helped the birdie make a new nest. The birdie was so happy and said, "Thank you so much for helping me. You're my new friend."

The little girl smiled and said, "I'm happy to help. Now go to sleep in your new nest and have sweet dreams."

Jack was so happy and replied, "Yes, I want to be your friend! Can you show me how to jump like you?"

The dolphin smiled and said, "Sure, let's practice together!" So they spent the whole day jumping and clapping their fins together. From that day on, Jack and the dolphin were the best of friends and sailed together every day.

"Ben, wait, don't do it!" Anna shouts. She follows him with Max, but she is too late. Ben climbs up the ladder and sits on the slide. He smiles and waves at Anna.

"Here I go!" He says, and pushes himself down the slide.

Sam and Lily were twins who loved to play on the beach. They liked to build sand castles, collect shells and splash in the water. One day, they saw a big boat with a sail and many people on it. They wondered what it was.

"Look, Lily, a boat!" Sam said.

"Where are they going?" Lily asked.

"Maybe they are going to the sea," Sam guessed.

"What is the sea?" Lily wondered.

Sam thought for a moment. He remembered what their mom had told them once. "The sea is a big, big water that goes on and on. It has many fish and plants and rocks in it. It is very old and beautiful," he explained.

Lily nodded. She tried to imagine the sea. She thought it must be very different from the beach. She wanted to see it. "Can we go to the sea, Sam?" she asked.

Sam shrugged. He didn't know how to go to the sea. He looked at the boat again. He saw a man with a hat and a beard waving at them. He waved back. "Maybe he knows how to go to the sea," he said.

"Let's ask him," Lily said.

They ran to the edge of the water and shouted at the man. "Hello, sir! Can you take us to the sea?" they asked.

The man smiled and shouted back. "Hello, children! I'm sorry, but I can't take you to the sea. This boat is very ancient and it can only go to the island. The island is very nice, but it is not the sea. The sea is far, far away. You need a bigger and faster boat to go to the sea," he said.

Sam and Lily felt sad. They wanted to go to the sea, but they didn't have a bigger and faster boat. They thanked the man and waved goodbye. They went back to their sand castle and played with their shells. They hoped that one day, they would see the sea. They knew it was very old and beautiful. They wanted to understand it.

Lily loves pandas. She has a big panda toy that she holds every night. She calls her panda Po. Po is soft and black and white. Lily likes to hug Po and tell him stories.

One day, Lily goes to the zoo with her mom and dad. She is very excited to see the real pandas. She holds Po in her arms and runs to the panda exhibit. She sees two pandas eating bamboo and playing. They are cute and fluffy.

"Look, Po, they are like you!" Lily says to her toy. "Do you want to say hello?"

Lily tries to climb over the fence to get closer to the pandas. But her mom stops her.

"No, Lily, you can't do that. The pandas are wild animals. They might hurt you or Po. You have to stay behind the fence and watch them from a distance." Her mom says.

"But I want to play with them. They are my friends." Lily says.

"I know, sweetie, but they are not toys. They have their own home and family. They are very organized. They have rules and routines. They don't like strangers. You have to respect them and their space." Her mom explains.

Lily feels sad. She doesn't understand why she can't play with the pandas. She holds Po tighter and looks at the pandas with longing.

"Maybe one day, Po, we can visit them in their home. Maybe they will let us play with them then. Maybe they will like us." She whispers to her toy.

She hopes that the pandas can hear her and smile. She hopes that they are happy and safe. She hopes that they are her friends.

Lila and Ben were playing with marbles in the park. They had many marbles of different colors and sizes. They liked to roll them on the ground and see who could get the most in a circle.

"Look, I have a big blue marble!" Lila said, holding it up. "It is very pretty and shiny."

"I have a small red marble!" Ben said, showing his. "It is very fast and smooth."

They rolled their marbles and tried to knock each other's out of the circle. Lila's blue marble hit Ben's red marble and made it fly away.

"Ha, I win!" Lila said, smiling. "Give me your red marble, Ben. It is mine now."

Ben frowned and looked at his red marble. He liked it very much and did not want to give it to Lila.

"No, I don't want to give you my red marble!" Ben said, holding it tight. "It is my favorite marble. You can't have it."

"Yes, you have to give it to me!" Lila said, reaching for it. "That is the rule. If I knock your marble out, you have to surrender it to me."

They started to pull and tug on the red marble. They both wanted it and did not want to share.

"Stop, stop!" a voice said. It was Mom, who was watching them from a bench. "What are you doing, Lila and Ben? Why are you fighting over a marble?"

They looked at Mom and let go of the red marble. They felt ashamed and sorry.

"We were playing with marbles, Mom," Lila said. "But I knocked Ben's marble out and he did not want to surrender it to me."

"I did not want to surrender it to Mom, because it is my favorite marble," Ben said. "It is different from all the other marbles. It is special to me."

Mom nodded and smiled. She understood how they felt. She picked up the red marble and held it in her hand.

"I see, I see," Mom said. "It is a very nice marble, Ben. And so is your blue marble, Lila. But you know what? Marbles are more fun when you play with them together, not when you fight over them. How about you share your marbles and take turns using them? That way, you can both enjoy them and be happy."

Lila and Ben thought about what Mom said. They realized she was right. They did not want to fight over marbles. They wanted to play with them and have fun.

"Okay, Mom," Lila said. "I'm sorry, Ben. I will share my blue marble with you. You can use it next time."

"Okay, Lila," Ben said. "I'm sorry, too. I will share my red marble with you. You can use it now."

They hugged each other and smiled. They thanked Mom and gave her a kiss. Then they picked up their marbles and went back to playing. They rolled them on the ground and saw how they sparkled in the sun. They were different, but they were beautiful. And they were happy.

Mia is a cat who likes to be independent. She does not like to share her toys, her food, or her bed with anyone. She likes to explore the house and the garden by herself, and sometimes she goes out for a long time.

One day, Mia meets a dog who lives next door. The dog is big and friendly, and he wants to play with Mia. He runs after her and barks, "Hello, cat! Do you want to be my friend? We can have fun together!"

Mia does not want to be friends with the dog. She thinks he is loud and annoying. She hisses and runs away, but the dog follows her. He tries to touch her with his paw, but Mia scratches him. "Ow, cat! Why are you so mean? I just want to play with you!" the dog cries.

Mia climbs up a tree and looks down at the dog. She says, "Go away, dog! I don't want to play with you. I want to be independent. I don't need anyone. Leave me alone!"

The dog feels sad and confused. He does not understand why Mia does not like him. He sits under the tree and looks up at her. He asks, "Cat, why are you so independent? Don't you get lonely? Don't you want to have a friend?"

Mia thinks about the dog's question. She remembers that sometimes she does get lonely, especially when it is dark and cold. She remembers that sometimes she does want to have a friend, someone who will listen to her and cuddle with her. She realizes that maybe being independent is not always good.

She looks at the dog and sees that he is not so bad. He is big and friendly, and he wants to play with her. He has a nice smile and a soft paw. Maybe he can be her friend.

She says, "Dog, I'm sorry for being mean to you. Maybe we can be friends. Maybe we can play together. But you have to be gentle and quiet. And you have to share your toys, your food, and your bed with me."

The dog is happy and surprised. He says, "Really, cat? You want to be my friend? I would love that! I will be gentle and quiet. And I will share everything with you. Come down from the tree and let's play!"

Mia comes down from the tree and lets the dog touch her with his paw. They sniff each other and wag their tails. They run and chase and roll in the grass. They have fun together.

Mia learns that being independent is good, but having a friend is better. She learns that sharing and caring are important. She learns that sometimes it is good to ask for help and to give help. She learns that the dog is her friend.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big tube near the slide. It was shiny and round and had a hole in the middle. They wondered what it was for.

"Let's carry it to the sandbox and make a tunnel!" Ben said. He was strong and brave and liked to try new things.

"OK, but be careful. It looks heavy and sharp," Lily said. She was compassionate and careful and liked to help others.

They took turns to carry the tube to the sandbox. It was hard work, but they were happy. They dug a hole in the sand and put the tube inside. They crawled through the tube and pretended they were explorers.

"This is fun!" Ben said. "Let's go again!"

"Wait, I see something shiny in the tube. Maybe it's a treasure!" Lily said. She reached inside the tube and felt something cold and metal. She pulled it out and saw that it was a needle. It had blood on it.

"Ow! It hurts!" Lily cried. She dropped the needle and looked at her hand. It had a small wound that was bleeding. She felt scared and sick.

"Let me see!" Ben said. He ran to Lily and looked at her hand. He saw the needle and the blood. He felt sorry and worried.

"Who put that needle in the tube? That's not nice! That's dangerous!" Ben said. He hugged Lily and tried to comfort her.

"Let's go to the nurse. She will make it better," Lily said. She was brave and smart and knew what to do.

They got out of the tube and ran to the nurse's office. They told her what happened and showed her the needle and the wound. The nurse was compassionate and kind and helped them. She cleaned the wound and put a bandage on it. She called their parents and told them to come.

But it was too late. The needle had germs on it that made Lily very sick. She had to go to the hospital and stay there for a long time. She had to take medicine and get shots and feel pain. She missed Ben and the park and the tube. She was sad and lonely and afraid.

Ben missed Lily too. He felt guilty and angry and sad. He wished he never found the tube or the needle. He wished he could make Lily better. He wished he could play with her again. He was sorry and lonely and afraid.

The end.

Sara was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls in her bedroom, but her favorite one was Lily. Lily had long yellow hair, a pink dress and a fragile necklace that sparkled in the sun. Sara loved to brush Lily's hair, dress her up and talk to her.

One day, Sara's mom came into her bedroom and said, "Sara, it's time to clean up your toys. We have to go to the store soon." Sara did not want to stop playing with Lily. She said, "But mom, I'm having fun with Lily. Can we stay a little longer?" Sara's mom shook her head and said, "No, Sara, we have to go now. You can play with Lily later. Come on, put her in the toy box and let's go."

Sara was sad. She did not want to leave Lily in the toy box. She thought Lily would be lonely and scared. She hugged Lily and said, "Don't worry, Lily, I'll be back soon. I love you." She kissed Lily's cheek and put her gently in the toy box. She closed the lid and followed her mom out of the bedroom.

When Sara and her mom came back from the store, Sara ran to her bedroom. She opened the toy box and looked for Lily. But she could not find her. She saw other dolls, but not Lily. She felt a panic in her chest. She said, "Mom, where is Lily? I can't find her. She's gone!" Sara's mom came into the bedroom and said, "Oh, Sara, I'm sorry. I forgot to tell you. Your cousin Jake came over while we were out. He wanted to play with your dolls. He took Lily with him. He said he liked her necklace."

Sara felt a surge of anger. She said, "What? Jake took Lily? He can't do that. Lily is mine. He might break her necklace. It's fragile. I want Lily back. Now!" Sara's mom said, "Calm down, Sara. Jake is your cousin. He's just a little boy. He didn't mean to upset you. He'll bring Lily back tomorrow. He promised. He said he'll take good care of her. He said he'll make her smile."

Sara did not believe Jake. She did not think he could make Lily smile. She thought he would make her cry. She said, "No, mom, I don't want to wait. I want Lily back today. She's my best friend. I miss her. Please, mom, please, call Jake and tell him to bring Lily back." Sara's mom sighed and said, "Okay, Sara, okay. I'll call Jake and ask him to bring Lily back. But you have to be nice to him. He's your cousin. He likes you. He likes Lily too. He just wanted to play with her."

Sara nodded and said, "Okay, mom, okay. I'll be nice to Jake. But he has to give Lily back. And he has to say sorry. And he has to be careful with her necklace. It's fragile. It's precious. Like Lily." Sara's mom smiled and said, "Alright, Sara, alright. I'll call Jake right now. You wait here. I'll be back soon." She left the bedroom and picked up the phone.

Sara waited in her bedroom. She hoped Jake would bring Lily back soon. She hoped Lily was okay. She hoped Lily would smile again. She hoped Lily would forgive her for leaving her in the toy box. She hoped Lily would still love her. She hoped Lily would still be her best friend.

"My grandma made it for me," Lily said. "She is very good at knitting. She gave it to me for my birthday."

"What happened?" Lily cried. She picked up her sweater and ran to her mom.

"Mom, look at my sweater! It shrank! Who did this?"

Mom looked at the sweater and frowned. She saw a dark stain on it and smelled something bad.

"Oh, Lily, I'm sorry. I think your brother spilled some juice on your sweater and tried to wash it. But he put it in the hot water and the dryer. That made it shrink."

Lily was very sad and angry. She loved her sweater and now it was ruined. She went to find her brother and yelled at him.

"Tommy, you are mean! You ruined my sweater! Grandma made it for me and you shrank it! How could you?"

Tommy was hiding under his bed. He heard Lily and felt sorry. He didn't mean to shrink her sweater. He wanted to clean it and make it nice again. But he didn't know how to wash clothes. He was scared of Lily and mom.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Tommy said. "I didn't know it would shrink. I was trying to help. Please don't be mad at me."

Lily looked at Tommy and saw his sad face. She remembered that he was her brother and she loved him. She also remembered that grandma was very good at knitting. Maybe she could make another sweater for her.

"It's okay, Tommy," Lily said. "I'm still mad, but I forgive you. Next time, ask mom before you wash anything. And maybe grandma can make me a new sweater. But you have to say sorry to her too."

Tommy nodded and hugged Lily. He said sorry to her and mom and grandma. Lily hugged him back and smiled. She still liked her sweater, even if it was small. Maybe she could give it to her doll. Or maybe she could ask grandma to make a matching one for Tommy. Then they could both wear their sweaters and be happy.

"Are you ready?" Jill asked Tom.

"Yes, I am. Are you?" Tom said.

"Of course. On your mark, get set, go!" Jill shouted.

They both ran as fast as they could. Jill was wearing her fancy dress and shoes that she got for her birthday. She felt very pretty and happy. Tom was wearing his old jeans and sneakers that he wore every day. He felt very comfortable and free.

Jill was ahead of Tom at first, but soon she felt her dress getting in the way. It was too long and too tight. She tripped over it and fell to the ground. She scraped her knee and tore her dress. She started to cry.

Tom saw Jill fall and stopped running. He ran back to her and helped her up.

"Are you okay, Jill?" Tom asked.

"No, I'm not. I hurt my knee and I ruined my dress. I can't race anymore." Jill said.

"I'm sorry, Jill. It's okay. You don't need a fancy dress to race. You just need to be yourself. You are still my best friend." Tom said.

He gave her a hug and a band-aid. They walked to the hill together and watched the sunrise. They smiled and held hands.

The moral of the story is: Don't let your clothes or appearance stop you from doing what you love. Be yourself and be kind to others.

One night, Anna had a special prayer. She wanted to ask God for a puppy. She loved puppies very much, but her mom and dad said they were too busy to take care of one. Anna prayed with all her heart that God would send her a puppy for her birthday, which was in two weeks.

The next day, Anna went to school. She had a lot of fun with her teacher and her classmates. They learned about numbers, colors, and animals. They also sang songs and played games. Anna was happy, but she still wished for a puppy.

She looked around and saw a lady standing by the sign. She smiled at Anna and said, "Hello, sweetie. Do you like the puppies? They need a good home. You can have one if you want."

Anna could not believe her ears. She looked at the lady and said, "Really? Can I have one? Please, please, please!"

The lady nodded and said, "Of course. You can choose any one you like. They are all very friendly and healthy. They just need some love and care."

Anna thanked the lady and hugged her. Then she looked at the puppies and picked the gray one. It was the smallest and the cutest. It snuggled in her arms and made a happy sound. Anna felt warm and fuzzy inside. She knew God had answered her prayer.

She ran home with the puppy and showed it to her mom and dad. They were surprised and happy for her. They agreed to let her keep the puppy, as long as she promised to feed it, walk it, and clean it. Anna said yes to everything. She named the puppy Lucky, because he was her lucky gift.

That night, Anna prayed again. She thanked God for the puppy and for the lady who gave it to her. She also thanked God for her birthday, which was the best day of the year. She kissed Lucky and cuddled with him. They fell asleep together, feeling warm and loved.

Sam and his mom went to the subway to go to the park. Sam liked the subway. It was big and fast and loud. He saw many people and things on the subway. He wanted to mark them with his crayon.

"Mom, can I mark the subway?" Sam asked.

"No, Sam, you can't mark the subway. That is not nice. The subway is not yours to mark. You can mark your paper or your book, but not the subway," Mom said.

"But I want to mark the subway. It is fun. Look, I can mark the seat and the window and the door," Sam said. He took out his crayon and started to mark the subway.

"Sam, stop that right now. You are making a mess. You are not being helpful. You are being naughty. Give me your crayon," Mom said. She took the crayon from Sam and put it in her bag.

Sam was sad and angry. He did not like Mom. He did not want to go to the park. He wanted to mark the subway.

"Mom, I'm sorry. I just wanted to mark the subway. I like the subway. Can I have my crayon back?" Sam said.

Mom looked at Sam. She saw that he was sorry. She also liked the subway. She understood that Sam was curious and creative. She wanted to be helpful.

"Sam, I know you like the subway. I like it too. But you can't mark the subway. It is not yours to mark. It is for everyone to use and enjoy. If you mark the subway, you are making it dirty and ugly. You are not being helpful. You are being rude. Do you understand?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom, I understand. I don't want to be rude. I want to be helpful. I'm sorry I marked the subway. Can I help you clean it?" Sam said.

Mom smiled. She was proud of Sam. He was learning to be helpful. She gave him a wet wipe and showed him how to clean the marks he made on the subway.

"Thank you, Sam. You are being very helpful. You are making the subway nice and clean again. You are being a good boy. I love you," Mom said.

"I love you too, Mom. Can we go to the park now?" Sam said.

"Yes, Sam, we can go to the park now. And you can mark your paper or your book there. But not the subway, okay?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. Not the subway. Only my paper or my book. I promise," Sam said.

They got off the subway and went to the park. They had a lot of fun. Sam marked his paper and his book with his crayon. He did not mark the subway. He was helpful. He was happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big rope hanging from a tree. They wanted to swing on it and have fun. Lily ran to the rope first and grabbed it. She said, "This is my rope. You can't have it."

Ben was angry. He wanted to swing on the rope too. He said, "No, it's not your rope. It's for everyone. Let me have a turn." He tried to pull the rope from Lily, but she held on tight. They both pulled and pulled, but neither of them would let go.

They started to yell and scream at each other. They did not hear the loud snap. The rope broke and they both fell to the ground. They hit their heads and their arms and their legs. They cried and cried. They were hurt and sad.

A lady came and saw them. She said, "What happened? Why were you fighting over the rope?" She helped them get up and took them to a bench. She said, "You should not be greedy and mean. You should share and be nice. The rope was not yours. It was for everyone. Now look what you did. You broke it and you hurt yourselves. You are very naughty."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry. We were wrong. We should have shared and been nice." They hugged each other and said, "We are sorry. We are friends." But the lady was still angry. She said, "You are too late. You can't play on the rope anymore. You have to go home now. And you have to tell your parents what you did. They will be very angry too."

Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want to go home. They did not want to tell their parents. They wished they had not fought over the rope. They wished they had been good. They squeezed each other's hands and walked away. They had a bad day.

"Yes, Tom, it is amazing!" Lily said.

But then, Ben came in. Ben was their big brother. He was envious of their tower. He wanted to knock it down.

"Hey, what are you doing?" Ben said. "That tower is silly. It is too tall. It will fall down."

"No, Ben, don't touch it!" Tom and Lily said. "We worked hard. We want to finish it."

"Ben, you are mean!" Tom said. "You ruined our tower!"

"Ben, you are bad!" Lily said. "You made us cry!"

Ben felt sorry. He saw that he had hurt his brother and sister. He wanted to make them happy again.

"I'm sorry, Tom and Lily," Ben said. "I was wrong. I was envious of your tower. It was very nice. Can I help you build it again?"

Tom and Lily looked at Ben. They saw that he was sincere. They decided to forgive him.

"Okay, Ben," Tom said. "You can help us. But you have to be careful and gentle."

"Okay, Lily," Ben said. "I will be. Thank you for giving me another chance."
