Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys in the living room. They have cars, trains, blocks and books. Sometimes they share, sometimes they fight.

One day, they see a cable on the floor. It is long and black and shiny. They do not know what it is for. They think it is a snake or a rope. They want to touch it and pull it.

"Look, Sam, a snake!" Tim says.

"No, Tim, a rope!" Sam says.

They run to the cable and grab it. They tug and twist and swing it. They laugh and scream and have fun.

But the cable is not a snake or a rope. It is a phone cable. It is connected to the phone on the table. The phone is old and heavy and has a ring. When Tim and Sam pull the cable, they make the phone fall off the table. It lands on the floor with a loud bang. It makes a noise like a bell.

"Ring, ring, ring!" the phone says.

Tim and Sam are scared. They drop the cable and run away. They hide behind the sofa. They think the phone is angry and wants to bite them.

"Who is it?" a voice says from the phone.

It is their mom. She is at work. She is calling to check on them. She hears the bang and the ring and the silence. She is worried and confused.

"Tim? Sam? Are you there? What happened?" she says.

Tim and Sam do not answer. They are too afraid. They hug each other and shiver. They feel uncomfortable and sorry. They wish they did not play with the cable. They wish they listened to their mom and did not touch the phone. They hope she is not mad at them. They hope she comes home soon.

Lily and Ben were playing at the park. They liked to go on the slide, the swings and the seesaw. But they did not like the big hill. It was too high and steep for them. They were fearful of the big hill.

One day, a new boy came to the park. His name was Sam. He was very brave and liked to do daring things. He saw the big hill and said, "I want to go down the big hill on my bike. It will be fun and fast."

Lily and Ben watched him as he rode his bike up the big hill. They thought he was crazy. They said, "Don't do it, Sam. It is too dangerous. You will fall and hurt yourself."

But Sam did not listen. He said, "I am not scared. Watch me." He reached the top of the hill and started to go down. He went very fast and made loud noises. He looked happy and proud.

But then, something bad happened. Sam saw a big rock on the path. He tried to avoid it, but he could not. He hit the rock and lost control of his bike. He screamed and fell off his bike. His bike kept going and hit the slide. It made a loud bang and broke the slide.

Lily and Ben ran to Sam. They saw that he was bleeding and crying. They felt sorry for him. They said, "Are you okay, Sam? Do you need help?"

Sam said, "I am not okay. I am hurt and scared. I wish I did not go down the big hill. I wish I could reverse what I did. I am sorry I broke the slide."

Lily and Ben said, "It's okay, Sam. We all make mistakes. We will help you. Come on, let's go to the nurse. She will make you feel better. And maybe we can fix the slide later."

They helped Sam get up and walked with him to the nurse. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that being brave is good, but being careful is better. And they learned that being friends is the best.

Sam liked to help his mom in the kitchen. He was an obedient boy who did what his mom told him. One morning, his mom asked him to tie his apron before making toast. Sam nodded and tried to tie his apron, but he did not know how. He made a big knot that was hard to undo.

His mom saw him and smiled. She said, "Don't worry, Sam. I will show you how to tie your apron. It is easy. You just need to make a loop, a cross, and a pull." She took his apron and untied the knot. Then she tied it again, slowly and clearly, so Sam could see. She repeated the words, "Loop, cross, pull."

Sam watched and listened. He wanted to learn how to tie his apron. He said, "Can I try, mom?" His mom said, "Of course, Sam. You are a smart boy. You can do it." She gave him his apron and helped him make a loop, a cross, and a pull. Sam felt proud when he tied his apron by himself.

Then he and his mom made toast. They put bread in the toaster and waited for it to pop. They spread butter and jam on the toast and cut it into triangles. They put the toast on a plate and brought it to the table. Sam's dad and sister were waiting for breakfast. They said, "Wow, Sam, you made toast with mom. You are a big helper. And you tied your apron too. You are a good boy."

Sam smiled and said, "Thank you, dad. Thank you, sis. I like to help mom. I like to tie my apron. I like to make toast. I like to eat toast. Toast is yummy." He took a bite of his toast and enjoyed it. He was happy and hungry. He was an obedient boy who liked to learn new things.

Lily likes to sing. She sings when she wakes up, when she plays, and when she helps her mom. She sings happy songs, silly songs, and made-up songs. She sings with her toys, her cat, and her dad.

One day, Lily and her mom make a pie. They mix flour, butter, sugar, and apples in a big bowl. They roll out the dough and put it in a pan. They put the apple mix on top and cover it with more dough. They make a hole in the middle and put the pie in the oven.

Lily sings a pie song while they wait. She sings about how yummy the pie will smell, how hot the pie will be, and how sweet the pie will taste. She sings about how she will share the pie with her mom, her dad, and her cat. She sings about how she will eat the pie with a fork, a spoon, or her fingers.

The timer rings and the pie is done. Lily and her mom take it out of the oven and put it on a rack. They let it cool down a bit and then cut a slice for each of them. They sit at the table and enjoy the pie. Lily sings a thank you song to her mom for making the pie with her.

After they finish the pie, Lily and her mom tidy up the kitchen. They wash the dishes, wipe the counters, and sweep the floor. They put the leftover pie in the fridge for later. They hug each other and say they love each other. Lily sings a good night song to her mom and goes to bed. She dreams of more pies and more songs.

Sara and Lily were playing with their dolls in the garden. They liked to dress them up in pink clothes and make them talk. Sara had a pin that she used to make a bow for her doll's hair. Lily wanted the pin too, but Sara said no.

"Please, Sara, can I have the pin? It is so pretty and shiny. I want to make a bow for my doll too," Lily said.

"No, Lily, it is mine. You have to find your own pin. Go away," Sara said.

Lily was sad and angry. She looked around the garden and saw a big red flower. She thought it was a pin too, because it had a pointy thing in the middle. She ran to the flower and tried to pull it out.

But the flower was not a pin. It was a rose, and it had thorns. The thorns hurt Lily's hand and made her bleed. She cried out loud and dropped the flower.

Sara heard Lily's cry and saw her hand. She felt sorry for her and wanted to help her. She ran to Lily and said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I was mean to you. Here, you can have my pin. Let me save your hand."

But it was too late. The thorn had made a big hole in Lily's hand and she was losing a lot of blood. She felt dizzy and fell to the ground. Sara tried to stop the blood with her pin, but it did not work. She screamed for help, but no one came. She hugged Lily and cried. She wished she had shared her pin with Lily. She wished Lily was not hurt. She wished Lily was still alive.

Lily was a naughty girl. She did not like to eat her dinner. She only liked to eat candy and cake. She hid her dinner under the table or gave it to the dog. Her mom and dad were sad. They wanted Lily to be healthy and strong.

One day, Lily went to visit her grandma. Grandma made a yummy dinner for Lily. She made chicken, rice, carrots, and applesauce. Lily did not want to eat it. She wanted candy and cake. She said, "No, thank you, Grandma. I do not like this dinner."

Grandma was surprised. She said, "But Lily, this is a good dinner. It has protein, starch, vitamins, and fruit. They help you grow and learn and play. Don't you care about your body and your brain?"

Lily did not know what protein, starch, vitamins, and fruit were. She did not know what they did for her body and her brain. She said, "No, Grandma. I do not care. I only care about candy and cake."

Grandma was sad. She said, "Lily, that is not true. You do care. You care about your mom and dad, who love you and make you dinner. You care about your dog, who is your friend and needs food too. You care about me, who wants to see you happy and healthy. And you care about yourself, who deserves to feel good and have fun. Candy and cake are nice sometimes, but they are not good for you all the time. They can make you sick and tired and grumpy. Eating a good dinner is one way to show that you care."

Lily thought about what Grandma said. She looked at her dinner. She looked at Grandma. She looked at herself. She felt sorry for being naughty. She said, "I'm sorry, Grandma. You are right. I do care. I care about you and mom and dad and dog and me. I will try to eat my dinner. Can I have a little candy and cake after?"

Grandma smiled. She said, "Of course, Lily. You can have a little candy and cake after you eat your dinner. I'm proud of you for being brave and caring. I love you very much."

Lily hugged Grandma. She said, "I love you too, Grandma. Thank you for making me dinner. It is yummy after all." She ate her chicken, rice, carrots, and applesauce. She felt good and happy. She had a little candy and cake for dessert. She was not naughty anymore. She was a good girl.

Tom and Mia were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big river near their house. They wanted to see the water and the fish.

"Let's go to the river, Mia!" Tom said.

"OK, Tom, but we have to be careful. The water is fast and deep," Mia said.

They walked to the river and saw some rocks and sticks. They threw some rocks and sticks into the water and watched them splash and float. They also saw some fish swimming and jumping.

"Look, Mia, a big fish!" Tom said.

"Wow, Tom, it is big! Maybe it can grow bigger and bigger!" Mia said.

They wanted to touch the fish, but they did not know how. They saw a branch that was long and thin. They thought they could use it to catch the fish.

"Let's use this branch, Mia. We can put it in the water and hook the fish," Tom said.

"OK, Tom, but we have to be gentle. We don't want to hurt the fish," Mia said.

They took the branch and put it in the water. They tried to hook the fish, but the fish was too fast and smart. It swam away from the branch and hid under a rock.

"Come on, fish, don't be shy. We just want to play with you," Tom said.

"Maybe the fish is scared, Tom. Maybe we should leave it alone," Mia said.

They tried a few more times, but they could not catch the fish. They felt sad and tired. They decided to go back to their house.

They walked away from the river and saw some berries on a bush. They thought they could eat them and feel better.

"Look, Mia, some berries. They look yummy," Tom said.

"OK, Tom, but we have to be careful. Some berries are bad and bitter," Mia said.

They picked some berries and put them in their mouths. They tasted them and made a face.

"Yuck, Mia, these berries are bitter. They are not yummy at all," Tom said.

"Yuck, Tom, you are right. These berries are bitter. They make my tongue hurt," Mia said.

They spit out the berries and threw them away. They felt sad and thirsty. They decided to go back to their house.

They ran back to their house and saw their mom. She was smiling and holding a plate of cookies.

"Hi, Tom and Mia. How was your adventure?" she asked.

"Hi, mom. It was not good. We could not catch the fish and we ate bitter berries," Tom said.

"Hi, mom. It was not fun. The fish was too fast and the berries were too bitter," Mia said.

"I'm sorry, Tom and Mia. That sounds hard. But I'm proud of you for trying and being brave. Do you want some cookies and milk? They are sweet and good," mom said.

"Yes, mom. We want some cookies and milk. They are sweet and good," Tom and Mia said.

They hugged their mom and took some cookies and milk. They ate them and felt happy and full. They forgot about the river and the berries. They thanked their mom and told her they loved her. She kissed them and told them she loved them too. They smiled and went to their room to play. They had a good day after all.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big pot on the stove. It had a cover on it.

"What is in there?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Let's look," Ben said.

They took off the cover and saw some red sauce. It smelled good.

"Can we taste it?" Lily asked.

"Maybe. But be careful. It might be hot," Ben said.

They dipped their fingers in the sauce and put them in their mouths. It was very spicy. It burned their tongues and made them cough.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" they cried.

Mom heard them and came running. She saw the pot and the sauce on their fingers and face.

"What are you doing? That's chili! It's not for kids! It's very spicy!" she scolded.

She took them to the sink and rinsed their mouths with water. Then she gave them some milk and honey to soothe their throats.

She was very angry and sad. She had made the chili for Dad's birthday. Now it was ruined.

She sent Lily and Ben to their room. They had to stay there until Dad came home. They felt very sorry and bad. They wished they had not touched the pot.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big dog with a man. The man wore a hat and a coat. He was a guard. He watched the park and the people.

"Can we pet the dog?" Lila asked Tom.

"I don't know. Maybe we should ask the guard," Tom said.

They walked to the guard and the dog. The dog wagged its tail and licked its lips. It looked hungry.

"Hello, sir. Can we pet your dog?" Lila asked the guard.

The guard smiled and nodded. "Sure, you can. His name is Rex. He is very friendly. But be careful, he is also very hungry. He likes to eat bones and biscuits."

"Can we give him a biscuit?" Tom asked.

The guard reached into his pocket and took out a biscuit. He gave it to Tom. "Here, you can give him this. He will like it."

Tom held the biscuit in his hand and offered it to Rex. Rex sniffed the biscuit and took it gently. He crunched it and wagged his tail again.

"Thank you, sir. Thank you, Rex. You are a good dog," Lila said.

The guard replied, "You are welcome, kids. You are very polite. Enjoy the park. But don't go too far. Stay safe."

Lila and Tom nodded and waved. They petted Rex one more time and then ran back to their toys. They had fun in the park with the guard and the dog.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They pretended to be chefs and made soup with water and toys. They used a big pot and a big spoon. They stirred and tasted and laughed.

One day, Mom came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She was not happy. She said, "Lily and Ben, what are you doing? This is not a game. You could get hurt. The pot is hot and the spoon is sharp. You need to be careful."

Lily and Ben did not listen. They thought Mom was silly. They said, "We are chefs, Mom. We are making soup. It is yummy. Do you want some?" They held out the spoon with water and toys.

Mom tried to warn them. She said, "No, thank you. That is not soup. That is water and toys. You need to stop. You need to clean up. You need to play with something else."

Lily and Ben did not stop. They said, "No, Mom. We are having fun. We are not done. We want to play more." They turned away from Mom and kept stirring and tasting and laughing.

Mom was angry. She said, "Lily and Ben, you are not listening. You are being naughty. You are making a mess. You are wasting water and toys. You are not being chefs. You are being silly." She took the pot and the spoon from them and put them away. She said, "You need to go to your room. You need to think about what you did. You need to say sorry."

Lily and Ben were sad. They did not like to go to their room. They did not like to say sorry. They did not like to make Mom angry. They realized they were wrong. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were not careful. We were not nice. We will not do it again."

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you, Lily and Ben. I am glad you are sorry. I want you to be safe and happy. I want you to play with something else. Something that is fun and safe and attractive. How about some crayons and paper? You can draw your soup and your toys. You can be artists."

Lily and Ben smiled. They liked to draw. They said, "Yes, Mom. We want to be artists. We want to draw our soup and our toys. We want to show you our pictures. We want to make you proud."

Mom smiled too. She said, "I am proud of you, Lily and Ben. You are good twins. You are good artists. You are good listeners. You are good chefs too. But only with real food and real tools. And only with my help. OK?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "OK, Mom. We understand. We will be good. We will be careful. We will be happy. We love you, Mom."

Mom said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. Now go and have fun. And don't forget to clean up your mess."

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big swing. Anna wants to swing first. She says, "I want to swing. It is fun. You can swing later."

Ben does not agree. He has a different opinion. He says, "No, I want to swing too. We can swing together. It is more fun. You can share."

Anna and Ben start to argue. They do not listen to each other. They pull the swing. They are not happy.

A dog comes to the park. The dog is playful. He sees the swing. He thinks it is a toy. He runs to the swing. He jumps and bites the swing. He makes a loud noise.

Anna and Ben stop arguing. They look at the dog. They are surprised. They laugh. They say, "Look at the dog. He is silly. He likes the swing too."

They decide to share the swing. They take turns. They swing with the dog. They have fun. They are friends again.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play with toys and draw pictures. One day, they found a shiny coin on the floor. They wondered what they could do with it.

"Let's buy some candy!" Tom said. He liked candy very much.

"No, let's buy some stickers!" Lily said. She liked stickers very much.

They argued and argued. They could not agree on what to buy. They did not want to share the coin.

A man saw them and smiled. He had a big hat and a long coat. He looked like a magician. He walked up to them and said, "Hello, little ones. Do you want to see a magic trick?"

Lily and Tom stopped arguing. They liked magic tricks. They nodded and said, "Yes, please!"

The man took the coin from their hands. He said, "This is a very special coin. It has a symbol on it. Do you know what a symbol is?"

Lily and Tom shook their heads. They did not know what a symbol was.

"A symbol is a picture that means something. This symbol means luck. If you have this coin, you will have good luck. But if you lose it, you will have bad luck. Do you want to keep it or give it to me?"

Lily and Tom looked at each other. They wanted to keep the coin. They thought it would make them happy.

"We want to keep it!" they said together.

The man laughed. He said, "Are you sure? I can give you something better. I can give you this magic wand. It can do anything you want. You can make candy, stickers, toys, anything. All you have to do is say the magic word. Do you want to trade the coin for the wand?"

Lily and Tom looked at the wand. It was shiny and sparkly. It had a star on the end. They thought it would make them happier.

"We want the wand!" they said together.

The man smiled. He said, "Very well. Here you go. The magic word is 'abracadabra'. Say it and wave the wand. But be careful. The wand only works once. Use it wisely."

He gave them the wand and took the coin. He said, "Goodbye, little ones. Have fun with your magic wand."

He walked away, whistling.

Lily and Tom were excited. They held the wand and said, "Abracadabra!"

They waved the wand and waited. Nothing happened. They tried again and again. Still nothing.

They realized the wand was not magic. It was just a stick. They had been tricked. They had lost their coin. They had been foolish.

They felt sad and angry. They wished they had not traded the coin. They wished they had shared it. They wished they had not met the man.

They learned a lesson. They learned to be careful with strangers. They learned to be happy with what they had. They learned to be friends.

Tom and Sue like to play with words. They make up poems and say them to each other. Sometimes they rhyme, sometimes they don't. They have fun with words.

One day, they decide to have a contest. Who can say the longest poem? They take turns to say their poems. Tom says a poem about a cat. Sue says a poem about a dog. Tom says a poem about a hat. Sue says a poem about a frog.

They keep going. Their poems increase. They have more and more words. They talk very fast. They try to remember their poems. They want to win.

But then, they get stuck. They run out of words. They can't think of any more poems. They look at each other. They don't know what to say.

They start to laugh. They realize they are silly. They don't need to have a contest. They can just play with words. They hug each other. They are friends. They say, "Let's make up a new poem together!" They smile and start to say their words. They have fun with words.

Tom and Mia love their pet cat, Lily. Lily is soft and fluffy and likes to play with them. Sometimes, Lily sleeps on their bed and purrs. Tom and Mia are happy when they see Lily.

One day, Tom and Mia want to give Lily a treat. They find a can of tuna in the kitchen. They know Lily likes tuna. They open the can and put some tuna in a bowl. They call Lily to come and eat.

But Lily does not come. They look for Lily in the living room, in the bathroom, in the closet. They cannot find Lily. They are sad and worried. Where is Lily?

They hear a meow from the window. They run to the window and see Lily on the roof. Lily is stuck on the roof. She cannot get down. She is scared and hungry. She meows again.

Tom and Mia want to help Lily. They get a chair and put it near the window. Tom climbs on the chair and tries to reach Lily. But Lily is too far. Tom cannot reach Lily. He says, "Lily, come here! I have tuna for you!"

Lily hears Tom and sees the tuna. She wants the tuna. She walks slowly to the edge of the roof. She stretches her paw and tries to reach Tom. But Tom is too far. Lily cannot reach Tom. She says, "Meow, meow!"

Tom and Mia have an idea. They get a blanket and hold it under the window. They say, "Lily, jump! We will catch you!"

Lily looks at the blanket and at Tom and Mia. She trusts them. She jumps from the roof and lands on the blanket. Tom and Mia catch Lily and hug her. They are happy. Lily is happy. She licks their faces and purrs. They give her the tuna and she eats it. They say, "We love you, Lily!"

Lily says, "Meow, meow!"

Sara and Ben are excited. Today is the day they enter the big hall. The big hall is where they have their music class. They love music class. They can sing, play, and dance with their friends.

They hold hands and walk with their teacher to the big hall. They see a big door. The teacher opens the door and says, "Come on, children, let's enter the big hall."

Sara and Ben enter the big hall. They see a lot of things. They see a big piano, a big drum, a big guitar, and a big xylophone. They also see a lot of small things. They see small bells, small shakers, small flutes, and small tambourines. They see their friends sitting on the floor.

Lily and Tom were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were animals. Lily was a cat and Tom was a dog. They chased each other around the sofa and the table.

"Meow, meow, I am a smart cat. You can't catch me, woof, woof," Lily said.

"Ruff, ruff, I am a fast dog. I will catch you, meow, meow," Tom said.

They ran and jumped and had fun. But they did not see the vase on the shelf. The vase was big and blue and shiny. Mom liked the vase very much. She said it was a gift from Grandma.

Lily and Tom bumped into the shelf. The vase wobbled and moved. It fell down and broke into pieces. Lily and Tom stopped playing. They looked at the vase. They felt scared and sad.

"Oh no, the vase! Mom will be mad at us," Lily said.

"What do we do? How do we fix it?" Tom said.

They tried to put the pieces together, but they could not. The vase was too broken. They heard Mom coming. They hid behind the sofa.

Mom saw the vase on the floor. She was shocked and angry. She looked for Lily and Tom.

"Lily, Tom, where are you? What happened to the vase?" Mom said.

Lily and Tom came out from behind the sofa. They looked at Mom with sorry eyes.

"Mom, we are sorry. We were playing and we broke the vase. We did not mean to. We tried to fix it, but we could not. We are very sorry," Lily and Tom said.

Mom sighed and knelt down. She hugged Lily and Tom.

"I know you are sorry. I know you did not mean to. But you have to be careful. The vase was very special to me. It was from Grandma. She is not here anymore. She gave it to me before she went to heaven. The vase reminded me of her," Mom said.

Lily and Tom felt more sad. They loved Grandma too. They missed her.

"Mom, we are sorry. We love Grandma too. We miss her. Can we do something to make you feel better?" Lily and Tom said.

Mom smiled and kissed them.

Lily and Tom nodded and smiled. They did what Mom said. They felt a little better. They learned a lesson. They still liked to play, but they were more careful. They did not break anything else. They loved Mom and Grandma and each other.

Ben and Mia were playing in the yard. They saw a big bird with brown feathers and a red thing on its neck. It was a turkey.

"Look, a turkey!" Ben said. "Let's feed it some bread."

They ran to the house and got some bread. They broke it into small pieces and threw them to the turkey. The turkey ate the bread and made a funny sound.

"Gobble, gobble!" Mia said. "He likes the bread."

They went closer to the turkey and tried to pet it. But the turkey did not like that. It pecked Ben's hand with its beak. It hurt a lot.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. "The turkey bit me!"

Mia ran to get their mom. She came and saw Ben's hand. It was red and had a small cut.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Mom asked. "What happened?"

"The turkey bit me!" Ben said. "He was mean!"

Mom cleaned Ben's hand and put a band-aid on it. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. The turkey was scared. He thought you wanted to hurt him. He was trying to protect himself. You have to be careful with wild animals. They are not like pets."

Ben nodded. He felt better. He said, "I'm sorry, too. I didn't want to hurt the turkey. I wanted to be his friend."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's very nice of you, Ben. But sometimes, the best way to be a friend to a wild animal is to leave it alone. They need their space and their freedom. Do you understand?"

Ben and Mia said, "Yes, Mom. We understand."

They went back to the yard and watched the turkey from a distance. They waved to him and said, "Bye, bye, turkey. Have a good day." The turkey gobbled and flew away.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a purple doll that she liked very much. Ben had a red car that he liked very much. They were having fun, but they were also making a lot of noise.

"Shh, shh, shh!" their mom said. "You are too loud. Daddy is trying to relax. He had a hard day at work. He needs some quiet time."

They put away their toys and looked for something else to play with. Lily found a book with pictures of animals. Ben found a puzzle with shapes and colors. They sat on the floor and started to play.

They were still having fun, but they were also very quiet. They did not shout, or laugh, or bang, or crash. They only whispered, or smiled, or snapped, or matched.

Their mom was happy. She went to check on their dad. He was lying on the couch, with his eyes closed and his mouth open. He was snoring softly.

"Look, he is relaxing!" their mom said.

"Yes, he is. He looks funny." Lily said.

They giggled quietly. They were good kids. They loved their dad. They wanted him to relax. They went back to their play. They were quiet and happy.

One night, a boy named Tom could not sleep. He heard a sound outside his window. It was a loud sound, like a hoot. He was scared. He got out of his bed and went to his window. He saw a big bird on a tree. It was an owl.

"Who are you?" Tom asked the owl.

"I am an owl," the owl said. "I live in the woods. I come out at night. Who are you?"

"I am Tom," Tom said. "I live in this house. I sleep at night. But I could not sleep today. You made a sound."

"I am sorry," the owl said. "I did not mean to scare you. I was looking for food. I like to eat mice and bugs. Do you like to eat mice and bugs?"

"No, I do not," Tom said. "I like to eat bread and cheese and fruit. Do you want some?"

When they were done, Lily looked at her necklace. She was very proud of it. She said to her mom, "Look, mom, I complete the necklace for grandma. It is very fancy and pretty. Do you think she will like it?"

Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "I think she will love it, Lily. You did a great job. You are very creative and thoughtful. Let's put it in a box and wrap it with a ribbon. Then we can give it to her when we visit her tomorrow."

Lily nodded and helped her mom pack the necklace. She was very excited to see her grandma and give her the jewelry. She hoped her grandma would wear it and think of her. She loved her grandma very much.

Lily loved balloons. She liked to blow them up, tie them, and play with them. She had many balloons of different colors and shapes. She always kept them in her room, where they made her happy.

One day, Lily's mom said they had to go to the store. Lily wanted to bring her balloons with her, but mom said no. "You have to stay here, Lily. The balloons might pop or fly away outside. They are safer in your room. We will be back soon, okay?"

Lily felt miserable. She did not want to stay here without her balloons. She wanted to show them to everyone and have fun with them. She did not listen to mom. She grabbed her favorite balloon, a big red one, and ran outside. She thought mom would not notice.

But mom did notice. She saw Lily running with the balloon and called her name. "Lily, come back! You can't take the balloon outside! It's dangerous!" But Lily did not hear her. She was too excited.

Lily ran across the street, holding the balloon. She did not see the car coming. She did not hear the horn. She only felt a big bump and a loud pop. The balloon burst in her hand. She fell to the ground, crying.

Mom ran to Lily and hugged her. She was scared and angry. "Lily, why did you do that? You could have been hurt! You did not stay here like I told you! You were very naughty!"

Lily looked at mom with tears in her eyes. She was sorry and sad. She lost her balloon and made mom mad. She wished she had stayed here like mom said. She said in a small voice, "I'm sorry, mom. I love balloons. I wanted to play with them. I didn't mean to be naughty."

Mom kissed Lily and said, "I know, Lily. I love you. But you have to listen to me. I only want you to be safe and happy. You still have many balloons in your room. You can play with them later, when we get home. But you have to promise me to stay here and never run away again. Okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I promise. I will stay here and be good. Can I have a hug?"

Mom hugged Lily and said, "Of course, Lily. You can have a hug. And a kiss. And a cookie. Come on, let's go home."

One day, they decide to make a big square with the blocks. They put four blocks in a row, then four blocks on top, then four blocks on the side, then four blocks on the other side. They have a big square.

"Look, we made a big square!" Ben says.

"Yes, it is very big and nice!" Mia says.

They look at the square and smile. They are happy.

But then, Ben has an idea. He wants to joke with Mia. He takes one block from the square and hides it behind his back. He says to Mia:

"Hey, Mia, do you see the square?"

"Yes, I see it. It is right here." Mia says.

"No, it is not. It is gone!" Ben says.

He shows Mia his empty hand and laughs.

"Ha ha, I joked you! I took one block from the square. See?" He shows Mia the block behind his back.

Mia looks at the square and sees a hole. She is not happy. She is sad and angry.

"That is not funny, Ben. That is mean. You broke the square. You are a bad friend." Mia says.

She takes the block from Ben and puts it back in the square. She does not want to play with Ben anymore. She turns away from him.

Ben feels sorry. He did not want to make Mia sad and angry. He wanted to make her laugh. He says to Mia:

"I am sorry, Mia. I did not mean to be mean. I wanted to be funny. I like you. You are a good friend. Can we play again?"

Mia looks at Ben and sees his sorry face. She thinks for a moment. She says to Ben:

"OK, Ben. I forgive you. But do not joke me like that again. It is not nice. Let us play nicely. Do you want to make a circle with the blocks?"

Ben nods and smiles. He says to Mia:

"Yes, I want to make a circle with you. Thank you, Mia. You are a good friend too."

They hug and make a circle with the blocks. They are happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park and pick up leaves. One day, she saw a squirrel running around like crazy. She wondered why the squirrel was acting so strange.

As she kept playing, she noticed that some of the leaves on the trees were turning brown and falling off. She thought that maybe the squirrel was going crazy because it was hungry and couldn't find any good nuts to eat.

Lily decided to prevent the squirrel from going hungry by gathering some nuts and leaving them on the ground for the squirrel to find. The next day, when she went back to the park, she saw the squirrel happily munching on the nuts she had left. She felt happy knowing that she had helped prevent the squirrel from going hungry.

Lily said, "Yes, you can play with me. But this puzzle is very hard, Tom. Are you sure you can do it?"

Tom said, "Yes, I can do it. I am very good at puzzles."

So, Lily and Tom started to play with the puzzle. They were having so much fun, but suddenly Lily noticed something strange. She said, "Tom, why did you freeze? Are you okay?"

Tom said, "Yes, I am okay. I just can't find the last piece of the puzzle. Can you help me?"

Lily said, "Sure, I can help you. Let's find it together." They looked for the last piece and finally found it. Tom was so happy and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very modest." 

Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom. Let's play again soon." And they continued to play with their puzzle happily ever after.

"Maybe it's a treasure," Lila said.

"Maybe it's a monster," Tom said.

They dug and dug, but the root was very strong and deep. They got tired and dirty. They needed a break.

They went to the kitchen and asked Mom for some juice and cookies. Mom smiled and gave them some. She asked them what they were doing.

"We're trying to get a big root out of the ground," Lila said.

"Why?" Mom asked.

"We don't know. We wonder what it is," Tom said.

Mom looked out of the window and saw the hole and the root. She laughed.

"That's not a root, that's a branch. It's from the old tree that fell down last year. We cut it up and used it for firewood, but we left some pieces in the ground. They're not available for digging. They're part of the earth now."

Lila and Tom looked at each other. They felt silly. They had been digging a branch, not a root.

They finished their juice and cookies and thanked Mom. They went back to the garden and filled the hole with dirt. They decided to look for something else to play with. They still had a lot of fun.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a lot of toys, but her favorite was a big teddy bear. She hugged him and talked to him every day. She called him Ben.

One day, Lily's mom made a yummy meal for lunch. She put some soup, bread, cheese and fruit on a tray and brought it to Lily's room. She said, "Lily, it's time to eat. Come and have your meal. You can play with Ben later."

But Lily did not want to stop playing. She said, "No, mom. I want to play with Ben. He is hungry too. He needs a meal." She took the tray from her mom and put it on the floor. She gave some soup to Ben and said, "Here, Ben. Drink this. It will make you warm and happy."

But Ben was not a real bear. He was a toy. He could not drink the soup. The soup spilled on him and made him wet and sticky. Lily did not notice. She gave him some bread and cheese and said, "Here, Ben. Eat this. It will make you strong and healthy."

But Ben could not eat the bread and cheese. He was a toy. The bread and cheese crumbled on him and made him dirty and smelly. Lily did not notice. She gave him some fruit and said, "Here, Ben. Have this. It will make you sweet and juicy."

But Ben could not have the fruit. He was a toy. The fruit squished on him and made him soggy and stained. Lily did not notice. She was happy to share her meal with Ben. She said, "See, mom. Ben and I are having a great meal. We are full and satisfied."

But Lily's mom was not happy. She saw the mess on the floor and on Ben. She said, "Lily, what have you done? You have wasted your meal and ruined your toy. Ben is not a real bear. He does not need a meal. He needs to be clean and dry. You need to eat your meal and take care of your things."

Lily looked at Ben and saw how wet, dirty, smelly, soggy and stained he was. She felt sad and sorry. She said, "Oh, mom. I'm sorry. I did not know. I wanted to be nice to Ben. I love him so much."

Lily's mom hugged her and said, "I know, Lily. I love you too. But you have to learn to be sensible and responsible. You have to eat your meal and keep your toys in good shape. You can still love Ben, but you have to treat him like a toy, not like a real bear."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I understand. I will eat my meal and clean Ben. I will be more careful next time."

Lily's mom smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. I'm proud of you. Come on, let's go to the kitchen and get a new tray. And then we can wash Ben and put him in the dryer. He will be fine. He will still be your big teddy bear."

Lily and her mom went to the kitchen and got a new tray. They ate their meal and enjoyed it. Then they washed Ben and put him in the dryer. He came out clean and fluffy. Lily hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I love you. You are my best friend."

Ben did not say anything. He was a toy. But he felt warm and cozy in Lily's arms. He was happy to be her big teddy bear.

The moral of the story is: You should eat your meal and take care of your toys. You can love them, but you have to treat them right.

One day, he saw a tidy house with a big garden. He was curious and wanted to explore. He soared down and landed on the fence. He saw a door with a sign that said "Bunny". He thought that maybe there was a friend inside. He knocked on the door and said, "Hello, can I come in?"

A voice from inside said, "Who are you and what do you want?" Sam said, "I am Sam, a fox who likes to soar. I saw your house and wanted to say hi. You have a nice garden."

The voice said, "I am Ben, a bunny who likes to dig. I don't like foxes. They are mean and hungry. Go away or I will call my dog."

Sam was sad and confused. He did not want to be mean or hungry. He just wanted to make a new friend. He said, "I am not mean or hungry. I just ate some berries. I don't want to hurt you. I want to play with you. Can we be friends?"

The voice said, "No, we can't be friends. You are a fox and I am a bunny. We are different and we don't get along. Now go away or I will call my dog."

Sam felt hurt and angry. He did not like to be rejected and yelled at. He thought that Ben was rude and silly. He said, "Fine, I don't want to be your friend either. You are a bunny and I am a fox. We are different and we don't get along. I will go away and I don't care about your dog."

He turned around and jumped off the fence. He wanted to soar away and forget about Ben. But he did not see the dog that was hiding behind the bushes. The dog saw Sam and barked loudly. He ran after Sam and tried to catch him. Sam was scared and ran as fast as he could. He wished he had not come to the tidy house. He wished he had stayed in the sky. He learned a hard lesson that day. Sometimes, curiosity can lead to trouble.

At last, the palace was beautiful, the way it was meant to be. Anna was so proud of her work. Everyone could see the palace had been cleaned.

Now, every day Anna was able to enjoy how clean and sparkly the palace was. And whenever it started getting a little bit messy, she knew just what to do - spray, spray, spray!

Once upon a time there was a monkey named Bo. Bo was always very tidy. One day, Bo was sitting in a tree when he noticed a string hanging from the branch. Bo reached out and pulled it, and a big surprise came tumbling down! It was a giant box, with lots of fun things inside. Bo opened it up and saw a bunch of toys, all so shiny and new.

"Oh wow, what are all these things?" Bo said. 

Suddenly, Bo heard a voice coming from inside the box.
"Hello! I'm a magic fairy, and I'm here to reward you for being so tidy," said the magical creature. 

The fairy pulled out a special toy. It was a shiny blue monkey. Bo was so happy, he hugged the toy tight.

"Thank you magical fairy," said Bo, as the fairy disappeared in a puff of sparkling stars.

Bo was so delighted with his new toy, he took it everywhere with him. He even named it - Mr. Tidy Monkey. 

Bo and Mr. Tidy Monkey were the best of friends. Together they traveled all around, and everywhere they went, they were sure to be tidy and kind.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy, daddy, and a little girl. The little girl's name was April. April was very excited. She was going to the airport with her parents. Daddy urged her to hurry up and get her coat on. April couldn't wait!

Once they arrived at the airport, it was very busy and loud. There were lots of people coming and going. Mommy pointed out all the fine airplanes flying in the sky. April had never seen an airplane before. She wished she could fly in one too!

Suddenly, the mommy and daddy started to argue. April didn't understand why. Mommy said she wanted to stay but Daddy urged her to leave. April was so confused. She wanted to stay at the airport too.

But in the end, mommy and daddy hugged each other as they said goodbye. April was glad. Soon, the mommy and daddy hugged April too and promised her that they would all go back to the airport again soon. April was happy, the airport was fun and she would definitely come back again!

Once upon a time, little Tommy was playing outside with his sticks and stones. He wanted to find something exciting and pulled on some tall grass to see if he could find anything hidden. Suddenly, he spotted a silver necklace sparkling in the sunlight! He was so excited and he quickly picked it up and started to pull on the necklace around his neck. 

Just then his mom, who had been watching nearby, shouted out "Tommy, stop pulling on that necklace, it's too fragile". 

Tommy looked to his mom, with a puzzled look on his face, "Why, Mom?" he asked. 

"Well, because if you keep pulling on it, it'll break and then you won't have it anymore," Mom replied. 

Tommy then realized he needed to be careful with the necklace and he thought about how he could keep it safe, he decided to hide it under his pillow. 

This story teaches us that sometimes, it's important to be careful with the things we find. By being careful and hiding the necklace, Tommy was able to keep it safe and keep it for a long time.

Once upon a time, there was a small, hairy mouse. The mouse liked to explore, so he headed out into the world. Suddenly, the ground under him began to shake and disappear, like a line being wiped away! He quickly scrambled to safety, but he couldn't figure out why the ground had disappeared. 

A little while later, he saw a small creature that looked like a cat. Staring at the mouse with piercing, green eyes, the creature spoke in a deep, quiet voice.

"Do you know why the ground disappeared?", it asked.

The mouse shook his head. 

"When I look around, I see things that are too big or too small. Sometimes, things just vanish away. Don't worry, soon the ground will pop back up again!" 

The mouse thanked the cat creature, before scurrying away. Sure enough, when he looked back the ground was back! He went home happy, knowing that sometimes things just disappear.

"You're welcome, Lily. You will be well soon. Just follow my advice. And call me if you need anything. I am always here to help." The doctor said.

"Thank you, boys," the bird said. "You are very kind. You saved my life. I was sick and could not find food or water. You gave me a good taste and made me strong again."

They found the hippo pool and ran to the fence. They saw a big hippo in the water. He was very fat and had a big mouth. He looked sleepy and bored.

"Hello, hippo!" Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The hippo did not answer. He just yawned and showed his teeth.

"Wow, he has big teeth!" Ben said. "Can he bite us?"

"No, he can't," mom said. "He is a herbivore. That means he only eats plants. But he can still be dangerous, so don't go too close to the fence."

Lily and Ben nodded. They watched the hippo splash in the water. They noticed a bad smell.

"Mom, what is that smell?" Lily asked. "It is very smelly!"

Mom laughed. "That is the hippo's poop. He poops in the water to mark his territory. That means he tells other hippos that this is his pool."

"Yuck!" Ben said. "That is gross!"

Lily and Ben made faces. They decided they did not like the hippo so much. They wanted to see other animals.

"Can we go now, mom?" Lily asked. "We want to see the penguins. They are cute and not smelly."

"Sure, let's go," mom said. "Maybe the hippo will be more friendly next time."

They waved goodbye to the hippo and walked away. The hippo did not care. He was happy to be alone in his smelly pool. He had gained a lot of weight from eating plants. He was the biggest and strongest hippo in the zoo.

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl named Hoot. Hoot loved to sit in his tree and watch the world go by. One day, he saw a little girl named Lily picking cherries from a tree. 

"Hello there, little girl," Hoot said. "What are you doing?"

"I'm picking cherries," Lily said. "Do you want one?"

Hoot thought for a moment. "I do like cherries, but I have a problem. When it gets cold, I freeze and can't move."

Lily had an idea. "I'll bring you some cherries to eat when it gets cold. That way, you won't have to move and you can still enjoy them!"

Hoot was very grateful. "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind."

From that day on, Lily would bring Hoot cherries whenever it got cold. Hoot was very happy and felt very wise for having such a clever friend.

"These doves need some water, Amy. We must find a way to keep them wet." 

Amy brightened up. She ran around the market until she found a bucket of water. Then, she carefully used the water to wet the doves feathers. 

As the sun went down, Amy proudly sold all the doves. Mommy was proud of how Amy found a way to make the doves look beautiful. 

After they went home, Amy fell asleep with a big smile on her face.

As they were mixing the ingredients, Lily noticed that the dough was turning brown. She was excited to see how the cookies would turn out. While they were waiting for the cookies to bake in the oven, Lily and her mom listened to their favorite song. They sang and danced around the kitchen.

Finally, the cookies were ready. They came out of the oven smelling delicious. Lily's mom let her have one cookie. It was warm and gooey, and tasted so good. Lily was happy that she had helped her mom bake cookies and that they had listened to music together.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy boat in the pond. They liked to pretend they were sailors and go on adventures. They made the boat go fast and slow, left and right, and sometimes splash the water.

"Look, Ben, I see a duck!" Lily said, pointing to a big white bird. "Let's go say hello!"

"Okay, Lily, but be careful. Ducks can bite!" Ben said, steering the boat towards the duck.

The duck saw the boat and quacked loudly. It did not like the boat in its pond. It swam closer and pecked at the boat. The boat tipped over and the water came in.

"Help, help!" Ben and Lily cried. "The duck is angry!"

A man who was walking by heard their cries. He was a real sailor and he wore a blue hat and a light jacket. He ran to the pond and picked up the boat and the children. He put them on the grass and dried them with his jacket.

"Are you okay, little ones?" he asked, smiling.

"Yes, thank you, mister!" Ben and Lily said, hugging the boat.

"You're welcome. I'm sorry the duck was mean to you. He was just protecting his home. Next time, be more careful where you sail your boat, okay?" the sailor said.

"Okay, we will. Thank you for saving us, sailor!" Ben and Lily said.

"You're welcome. Now, how do you feel?" the sailor asked.

"We feel wet and cold, but also happy and grateful!" Ben and Lily said.

"That's good. Now, let's go find your parents and get you some warm clothes and a hot drink, shall we?" the sailor said.

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said.

They followed the sailor to the park gate, where their parents were waiting for them. They told them what happened and thanked the sailor again. The sailor waved goodbye and went on his way. Ben and Lily learned a lesson that day: ducks can be friends, but also foes. And sailors can be heroes, but also friends.

Anna and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make cakes and pies. They used a big mixer to mix the flour and the eggs and the sugar. The mixer was loud and fast and made a funny noise.

"Look, Ben, our cake is ready!" Anna said. "Let's put it in the oven and wait for it to bake."

They put the cake in the oven and set the timer. Then they went to the window to see the sky. It was dark and cloudy. They heard a loud boom.

"What was that?" Ben asked.

"It was thunder," Anna said. "It means it will rain soon."

"Rain? I don't like rain. It makes everything wet and cold. And it makes me scared," Ben said. He looked worried.

Anna hugged him. "Don't be scared, Ben. Rain is not bad. It helps the plants grow and the birds drink. And it makes rainbows in the sky. Rain is fun. We can play with our boots and our umbrellas and splash in the puddles."

Ben smiled. "Really? That sounds fun. Can we do that after our cake is done?"

"Sure, we can. But we have to be careful and not catch a cold. And we have to share our cake with Mom and Dad. They will be happy to see what we made," Anna said.

They heard the timer beep. Their cake was done. They took it out of the oven and let it cool. It smelled good and looked yummy. They were proud of their work.

They put on their coats and their boots and their umbrellas. They went outside to play in the rain. They splashed in the puddles and laughed. They saw a rainbow in the sky. They were happy.

The moral of the story is: Rain can be fun and not scary. And it is good to share your work with others.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cries. "That hurts!"

Mia runs to help him. She sees a sign next to the squash. It says: "Do not touch. This is a prize for the best squash grower. It is very special and rare."

"Oh, Ben, you should have read the sign," Mia says. "This is not a toy. It is someone's hard work. You should be more careful and respectful."

Ben feels sorry. He says: "You are right, Mia. I was wrong. I should have asked before I touched. I hope I did not damage the squash."

They hear a voice behind them. It is a man with a big, hairy beard. He is the squash grower. He is not happy.

"Hey, what are you doing with my squash?" he says. "Did you kick it? Do you know how long it took me to grow it?"

Ben and Mia are scared. They say: "We are sorry, sir. We did not know. We thought it was a ball. We did not mean to hurt it."

The man looks at them. He sees that they are sincere. He says: "Well, I guess you did not know. But you should always ask before you touch something that is not yours. And you should always read the signs. They are there for a reason. Do you understand?"

Ben and Mia nod. They say: "Yes, sir. We understand. We will not do it again. We are very sorry."

The man smiles. He says: "It's okay. I forgive you. But you have to promise me something. Next time you come to the park, you will not touch my squash. You will only play with the things that are meant for playing. And you will also learn more about squashes. They are not balls. They are fruits. You can eat them. They are very tasty and healthy. Do you promise?"

Ben and Mia promise. They say: "Yes, sir. We promise. We will not touch your squash. We will play with the slide and the swing. And we will learn more about squashes. Thank you for teaching us."

The man says: "You are welcome. Now, go and have fun. But be careful and respectful."

Ben and Mia say: "Thank you, sir. Goodbye."

They run to the slide and the swing. They have fun. But they also remember the lesson they learned. They do not touch things that are not theirs. They read the signs. And they are curious about squashes. They ask their parents to buy some squashes and cook them. They try them and like them. They are happy and smart.

"Uh-oh, I think that is mom's ring," Ben said, feeling scared. "She must have dropped it when she was watering the flowers. We have to give it back to her. She will be very sad if she loses it."

"Okay, let's go find mom," Lily said, putting the ring on her finger. "Maybe she will let me wear it for a little while. It is so pretty."

They ran to the house, looking for their mom. They did not see her in the kitchen or the living room. They heard a noise from upstairs. They went up the stairs, calling her name.

Lily nodded and wiped her tears. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. I'm sorry I scared you. Next time, I will surrender sooner."

They walked home together, holding hands. They learned that playing is fun, but safety is important. They also learned that surrendering is not always bad, but sometimes it is smart and kind.

Tom is curious and scared. He asks, "What is an x-ray? How does it work?"

The doctor explains, "An x-ray is a kind of light that can see through your skin and bones. It shows us if your arm is broken or not. You have to stay very still while the machine makes a beep sound. Then we can look at the picture on a screen."

Tom nods and follows the doctor to the x-ray room. He lies on a table and puts his arm on a plate. The doctor covers him with a big apron and goes behind a window. He says, "Ready, Tom? Here we go. One, two, three, beep!"

Tom hears the beep and sees a flash of light. He does not feel anything. He waits for the doctor to come back. The doctor smiles and shows him the picture on the screen. He says, "Good news, Tom. Your arm is not broken. You just have a bruise. It will heal soon. You are a brave boy."

Tom is happy and relieved. He thanks the doctor and hugs his mom. He says, "I'm sorry I was clumsy, mom. I will be more careful next time."

His mom kisses him and says, "It's okay, Tom. I love you no matter what. But maybe you should wear a helmet when you ride your bike."

"Why?" Sam asked. "You have so many acorns in your nest. You don't need this one. I have very few acorns. I need this one."

Lily was very happy. She had a loose tooth. She wiggled it with her tongue. She wanted it to fall out. She knew that the tooth fairy would come and give her a coin.

She showed her tooth to her brother Max. He was older and had no loose teeth. He was not happy. He said, "That's not fair. Why do you get a coin and I don't? I want a loose tooth too."

Lily said, "Don't be mean, Max. You had loose teeth before. You got coins too. Now it's my turn. You have to accept it."

Max said, "No, I don't. I have an idea. I will take your tooth when it falls out. Then I will put it under my pillow. The tooth fairy will think it's mine. Then I will get a coin and you won't."

Lily said, "That's a bad idea, Max. That's not nice. The tooth fairy will know. She is very smart. She can see your teeth. She can see my teeth. She will know who the tooth belongs to. She will not give you a coin. She will be angry with you."

Max said, "No, she won't. She will not notice. She will be fooled. I will do it. You can't stop me."

Lily was sad. She did not want to lose her tooth and her coin. She did not want to fight with her brother. She did not know what to do.

That night, Lily's tooth fell out. She put it under her pillow. She went to sleep. She dreamed of the tooth fairy. She hoped she would come and give her a coin.

But Max was awake. He sneaked into Lily's room. He lifted her pillow. He saw her tooth. He took it. He ran to his room. He put it under his pillow. He smiled. He went to sleep. He dreamed of the coin.

But the tooth fairy was clever. She flew into the house. She saw Max's pillow. She saw the tooth. She knew it was not his. She saw Lily's pillow. She saw no tooth. She knew it was hers. She was not fooled. She was not happy.

She took the tooth from Max's pillow. She left a note. It said, "This is not your tooth. This is Lily's tooth. You are not nice. You are naughty. You get no coin. You have to say sorry."

She took the tooth to Lily's pillow. She left a coin. She left a note. It said, "This is your tooth. This is your coin. You are nice. You are good. You have a brilliant smile."

Lily was very happy. It was her birthday and she had a big cake and many balloons. She also had a present from her mom and dad. They said she would receive it after the cake. Lily wondered what it was. She hoped it was a doll or a book.

But when mom and dad brought the present, Lily was not happy. It was a clown. A big, scary clown with a red nose and a loud horn. Lily did not like clowns. They made her cry. She did not want the clown. She wanted a doll or a book.

"Surprise!" mom and dad said. "We hired a clown for your birthday. He will make you laugh and do tricks."

Lily did not laugh. She screamed. She ran to her room and slammed the door. She did not want to see the clown. She was angry and sad.

The clown felt bad. He did not mean to scare Lily. He wanted to make her happy. He knocked on the door and said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I'm not a bad clown. I'm a nice clown. Can I show you something?"

Lily did not answer. She hid under her bed. She did not trust the clown.

The clown tried again. He said, "Lily, I have something for you. A gift. It's not a clown. It's something you like. Please open the door."

Lily was curious. She wanted to see the gift. She opened the door a little bit. She saw the clown holding a box. He smiled and said, "Happy birthday, Lily. This is for you."

Lily opened the box. Inside was a doll. A beautiful doll with a pink dress and a bow. Lily loved the doll. She smiled and said, "Thank you, clown. You are a nice clown."

The clown was happy. He said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you like the doll. Can I show you some tricks now?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, clown. You can show me some tricks. But please don't honk your horn. It's too loud."

The clown agreed. He said, "OK, Lily. I won't honk my horn. I'll make you some balloons instead."

Lily and the clown became friends. They played with the doll and the balloons. They laughed and had fun. Lily forgot about the bitter cake. She had a happy birthday after all.

Lily liked to fold paper. She could make hats, boats, and birds with paper. She liked to show her paper things to her mom and dad. They smiled and said she was clever.

One day, Lily found a big red paper in the living room. It was on the armchair where mom liked to read. Lily thought it was a good paper to fold. She took it and started to make a big hat.

But the paper was not a paper. It was a book. It was mom's favorite book. Mom had a bookmark in it. She wanted to finish it later. Lily did not know that. She folded the book and made a hat.

Mom came back and saw the book hat. She was very sad and angry. She said, "Lily, what did you do? You ruined my book! That was not a paper to fold. That was a book to read. You should not take things that are not yours. You should ask first."

Lily felt sorry. She did not want to make mom sad and angry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I did not know it was a book. I thought it was a paper. I wanted to make a hat for you. I like to fold paper."

Mom hugged Lily and said, "I know you like to fold paper. And I know you wanted to make a hat for me. But you have to be careful with other people's things. Books are not papers. Books are stories. They have words and pictures. They are special. You have to respect them. You have to ask before you touch them. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I will not fold books again. I will ask before I touch things. I'm sorry I ruined your book. Can I help you fix it?"

Mom smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. That is very kind of you. I forgive you. We can try to fix the book together. And then we can read it together. Maybe you will like the story too."

Lily smiled and said, "I would like that, mom. I like stories too. And I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my clever girl. And you are learning to be a good girl too."

The moral value of the story is: respect other people's things and ask before you touch them.

Lily and Max were in the car with Mom and Dad. They were going to the zoo to see the animals. Lily was very excited. She wanted to see the lions and the monkeys and the elephants. Max was not so excited. He was scared of the loud noises and the big teeth. He held his teddy bear tight.

"Are you ready, kids?" Mom asked. "We're almost there."

"Yes, yes, yes!" Lily said, bouncing in her seat.

"No, no, no!" Max said, hiding his face.

Mom looked at Max and smiled. "Don't worry, honey. The animals are behind fences. They can't hurt you. And you have your teddy bear to protect you."

Max nodded, but he still felt nervous. He looked at his teddy bear and saw something shiny. It was a buckle on his bear's collar. He liked the buckle. It was smooth and round and made a click sound when he pressed it. He pressed it again and again. It made him feel calm.

They arrived at the zoo and got out of the car. Lily ran to the gate, pulling Dad by the hand. Max followed slowly, holding Mom by the other hand. He still had his teddy bear and his buckle.

They saw many animals. Lily stared at them with wonder. She pointed and shouted their names. Max stared at them with fear. He clutched and whispered to his bear.

They came to the lion enclosure. Lily ran to the fence, eager to see the king of the jungle. Max stayed back, afraid to see the king of the teeth. He pressed his buckle.

Suddenly, he heard a roar. It was loud and scary. It made him jump. He looked up and saw a big lion, staring at him with yellow eyes. He felt his heart beat fast. He wanted to run.

But then, he saw something else. He saw his teddy bear, staring back at the lion with brown eyes. He saw his buckle, shining in the sun. He heard his click, sounding in his ear. He felt his calm, spreading in his chest.

He smiled. He was not scared anymore. He had his teddy bear and his buckle. They were stronger than the lion.

He walked to the fence, holding his bear. He looked at the lion and said, "Hello, Mr. Lion. This is my teddy bear. He has a buckle. Do you want to see?"

The lion stopped roaring. He tilted his head. He looked at the bear and the buckle. He looked at the boy and the smile. He blinked. He nodded.

Lily and Mom and Dad came to join them. They saw Max and the lion, staring at each other. They saw the bear and the buckle, shining between them. They saw the smile and the nod, sharing a moment.

They smiled too. They were proud of Max. He had made a new friend.

Lily shook her head. "No, Ben, that's not nice. The fly wants to be free. And Grandma might not like a fly in her mail. She might get scared or angry."

Ben frowned. "But I want to mail something to Grandma. She lives far away and I miss her. What can we mail her?"

Lily thought for a moment. She saw a paper and some crayons on the porch. She had an idea.

"Let's draw a picture for Grandma. We can draw the fly and the flowers and us. We can write 'We love you, Grandma' on it. Then we can mail it to her. She will be happy to see our picture."

Ben liked Lily's idea. He smiled and nodded. "Okay, let's do that. That's a good thing to mail."

They ran to the porch and got the paper and crayons. They drew a colorful picture of the fly and the flowers and themselves. They wrote 'We love you, Grandma' with big letters. They folded the paper and put it in an envelope. They wrote Grandma's name and address on it.

They asked their mom to help them mail the picture. Their mom was proud of them. She said they were very sweet and thoughtful. She said Grandma would love their picture. She said she would take them to the mailbox later.

Ben and Lily hugged their mom. They were happy. They knew their picture would make Grandma happy too. They knew the mail was dependable. It would take their picture to Grandma safely and quickly. They hoped Grandma would mail them a picture back. They loved Grandma very much.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play pretend. They had a big box of costumes and toys that they used to make up stories. One day, they decided to be kings and queens of a nation. They put on crowns and robes and made a throne out of pillows.

"Welcome to our nation, where we make the rules!" Ben said.

"Yes, and we are very creative and kind!" Lily said.

They had fun making laws and giving orders to their stuffed animals. They also made a flag out of paper and crayons and hung it on the wall.

But then, their mom came in and saw the mess. She was not happy.

"Ben and Lily, what have you done? You have to clean up this room right now!" she said.

Ben and Lily did not want to clean up. They wanted to keep playing. So they lied to their mom.

"Mom, we can't clean up. We are sick. We have a fever and a cough and a sore throat," they said.

Their mom touched their foreheads and felt that they were not hot. She knew they were lying.

"Ben and Lily, that is not nice. You have to tell the truth. Lying is bad. And you are not sick. You are just lazy. Now you have to clean up and go to bed early. No more playing for today," she said.

Ben and Lily felt ashamed and sad. They had to put away their costumes and toys and take down their flag. They had to say sorry to their mom and go to bed. They had no more fun. They learned that lying was not creative or kind. It was only trouble.

Ben liked to swim in the pond with his big sister, Amy. They wore swimsuits and goggles and splashed in the water. Ben liked to pretend he was a fish and swim under the water. Amy liked to pretend she was a mermaid and swim on top of the water.

One day, they saw a big post in the pond. It was brown and hard and had a sign on it. Amy wanted to read the sign, but Ben did not. He wanted to swim around the post and see what was on the other side. He was stubborn and did not listen to Amy.

Amy swam to the post and looked at the sign. It said, "Danger! Do not swim past this post. There are sharp rocks and strong currents." Amy was scared and called for Ben. But Ben did not hear her. He swam past the post and felt the water pull him. He saw the sharp rocks and tried to swim back. But he could not. He was stuck.

Amy saw Ben in trouble and swam to help him. She grabbed his hand and pulled him away from the rocks. She swam with him to the shore and hugged him. She was angry and sad and said, "Ben, you were very stubborn and very silly. You could have been hurt. You should have read the sign and listened to me."

Ben was sorry and said, "Amy, you were very brave and very kind. You saved me. I should have read the sign and listened to you." He hugged her back and said, "I love you, big sister." Amy smiled and said, "I love you, little brother." They dried off and went home. They never swam past the post again.

Anna and Ben run to the kitchen. They see a big tray with a long bone, a bowl of water, and a bag of kibble. They want to help their mom feed Spot. Anna says, "I will give him the bone. He can chew it and have fun." Ben says, "I will give him the water. He can drink it and be happy."

They take the tray and go to the backyard. They see Spot wagging his tail and barking. He is excited to see them. Anna puts the bone on the ground and says, "Here you go, Spot. This is for you." Spot sniffs the bone and starts to gnaw on it. He makes loud noises and wags his tail more. Anna smiles and says, "He likes it, mom. He likes the bone."

Ben puts the bowl of water next to the bone and says, "Here you go, Spot. This is for you too." Spot looks at the water and licks it. He drinks some and then goes back to the bone. He makes softer noises and wags his tail less. Ben says, "He likes it, mom. He likes the water."

Mom comes to the backyard and sees Anna and Ben and Spot. She says, "You did a good job, Anna and Ben. You fed Spot and made him happy. He is a lucky dog to have you." Anna and Ben hug their mom and say, "We love you, mom. And we love Spot too." They all smile and watch Spot enjoy his food.

At the park, she saw a big rose bush. The roses were red, pink and yellow. They smelled nice and looked pretty. Lily wanted to touch one, but her mom said no.

"Roses have thorns, Lily. Thorns are sharp and can hurt you. You have to be careful with roses," her mom said.

Lily was curious. She asked, "What are thorns, mom?"

"Thorns are like little needles that grow on some plants. They protect the plants from animals that want to eat them. But they can also poke your skin and make you bleed," her mom explained.

Lily understood. She said, "Oh, I see. Thorns are bad for me, but good for roses. I will not touch them, mom. I will just look at them and smell them."

Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "That's right, Lily. You are a smart girl. You learned something new today. I am proud of you."

Lily was happy. She learned about roses and thorns. She also learned to listen to her mom and be careful. She enjoyed the rest of the day at the park with her mom. She saw more flowers, birds and swings. She had fun and learned more things. She was excited to go to the park again.

"Look, Tom, a slide! Let's go!" Sara says.

Tom is scared. He does not like high things. He hears his heart beat fast. He shakes his head.

"No, Sara, it is too high. I don't want to go. You can go if you want, but I will wait here," Tom says.

Sara is not scared. She thinks Tom is silly. She runs to the slide. She climbs the steps. She sits on the top. She looks down. She smiles. She slides down.

"Wow, this is fun!" Sara shouts.

But Sara slides too fast. She does not see a rock at the end of the slide. She hits the rock with her eye. She feels a lot of pain. She cries.

"Ow, ow, ow! My eye, my eye!" Sara cries.

Tom hears Sara cry. He runs to her. He sees her eye. It is red and swollen. He feels sorry for her. He hugs her.

"I'm sorry, Sara. Are you okay?" Tom asks.

Sara is not okay. She can not see well with her eye. She is sad and angry. She wishes she did not go on the slide.

"I'm not okay, Tom. My eye hurts. I can not see. I was stupid. I should have listened to you," Sara says.

Tom takes Sara to his mom. His mom calls Sara's mom. Sara's mom comes to the park. She takes Sara to the doctor. The doctor says Sara's eye will heal, but it will take time. Sara has to wear a bandage on her eye. She can not play for a while.

Sara learns a lesson. She learns to be careful and not to be too proud. She learns to listen to her friends and not to make fun of them. She says sorry to Tom. Tom forgives her. They are still friends. But Sara does not like slides anymore.

Tom was a tall man with a big mustache. He liked to rub his mustache when he was thinking or happy. He worked at a zoo, where he took care of many animals. He loved his job, but he had a problem. Some of the monkeys liked to pull his mustache and make him angry.

"Help! Help! Help!" Tom cried. "Someone get this monkey off me!"

"I want to put bananas in the cake," Tom said. "Bananas are yummy and soft."

"No, I want to put apples in the cake," Lily said. "Apples are crunchy and sweet."

They both grabbed the pan and pulled it hard. The pan was thin and it broke in half. Tom and Lily were sad and angry.

"Look what you did!" Tom shouted. "You broke our pan!"

"No, you did!" Lily shouted back. "You pulled too hard!"

They started to cry and yell at each other. Their mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw the broken pan and the twins.

"What happened here?" she asked. "Why are you fighting?"

Tom and Lily told her their story. They both blamed each other for the pan.

Mom sighed and hugged them. "I'm sorry your pan is broken, but you should not disagree so much. You are twins and you should share and be nice to each other. How about we make a real cake together, and we can put both bananas and apples in it?"

Tom and Lily liked that idea. They said sorry to each other and helped mom make the cake. They mixed the flour, the eggs, the sugar, the bananas and the apples in a big bowl. Then they poured the batter in a new pan and put it in the oven. They waited for the cake to bake and smelled the delicious aroma.

Soon, the cake was ready. Mom took it out of the oven and let it cool. Then she cut a big slice for Tom and a big slice for Lily. They ate the cake and smiled. It was the best cake ever. They agreed that bananas and apples were both good in the cake. They thanked mom and hugged her. They were happy and they did not fight anymore.

"Who are you?" Lily asked Max.

"I am a teacher. And you?" Max said.

"A hanger? Why did he steal a hanger?" Max asked.

"I don't know. Maybe he wanted to hang his coat. But he was very grumpy and rude. He pushed the lady who worked at the store and ran away." Lily said.

"That's not nice. We have to find him and tell him to say sorry." Max said.

They looked around the room for clues. They saw a hanger on the floor near the door. Lily picked it up and held it in front of her.

"Look, Max. I found the hanger. It has a red sticker on it. Maybe that's where he got it from." Lily said.

"Good job, Lily. You are a smart detective. Let's go to the store and see if we can recognize the bad guy." Max said.

They put on their shoes and went outside. They walked to the store and looked at the people inside. They saw a man with a big hat and a long coat. He was holding a hanger in his hand. He looked very grumpy.

"Max, look. It's him. It's the bad guy. He has the same hanger as us." Lily said.

"Let's go and talk to him." Max said.

They walked up to the man and tapped him on the shoulder.

"Excuse me, sir. We are detectives. We know you stole this hanger from the store. You have to say sorry to the lady and give it back." Lily said.

The man turned around and looked at them. He was surprised and confused. He was not the bad guy. He was their dad. He had bought the hanger for their mom.

"Lily? Max? What are you doing here? And why are you wearing my clothes?" He asked.

They looked at him and realized their mistake. They felt silly and embarrassed.

"Oops. Sorry, dad. We thought you were the bad guy. We were playing dress up and we found this hanger on the floor. We thought you stole it." Lily said.

"It's okay, kids. I didn't steal it. I paid for it. See, I have the receipt. And I'm not grumpy. I'm just tired. I had a long day at work." He said.

He smiled and hugged them. He gave them the hanger and told them to put it back in their room. He also bought them some ice cream and took them home. "Can I go first?" Lily asked Max.

"No, I want to go first!" Max said.

They started to argue and push each other. Their mom saw them and was not happy.

"Stop fighting, you two!" she said. "You can take turns on the slide. Lily, you go first, then Max. And be nice to each other."

Lily climbed up the ladder and slid down the slide. She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She smiled and said, "Whee! That was fun!"

Max watched Lily and felt jealous. He thought the slide was boring and he wanted something more exciting. He saw a big trunk near the slide. It was old and dirty and had a lock on it.

"I wonder what's inside," he thought. He left the slide and went to the trunk. He tried to open it, but it was too hard. He kicked it and banged it, but nothing happened.

"Hey, Max, come back to the slide!" Lily called. "It's your turn!"

"No, I don't want to slide!" Max said. "I want to open this trunk!"

He kept trying to open the trunk, but he only hurt his foot and his hand. He started to cry and felt sad.

Lily heard Max crying and went to see what was wrong. She saw him sitting on the ground, holding his foot and his hand.

"What happened, Max?" she asked.

"I tried to open the trunk, but I couldn't," he said. "It was too hard and I hurt myself. And I missed my turn on the slide."

Lily felt sorry for Max. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Max. The trunk is not for us. It belongs to someone else. Maybe there is nothing inside, or maybe there is something bad. We should leave it alone and play on the slide. The slide is fun and safe and we can share it."

Max nodded and said, "You're right, Lily. The slide is better than the trunk. I'm sorry I was mean to you. Can we still take turns on the slide?"

"Of course we can," Lily said. "Come on, let's go!"

They ran back to the slide and took turns sliding down. They laughed and had fun. Their mom saw them and was happy.

The moral of the story is: Don't be greedy and curious about things that are not yours. Be happy with what you have and share it with others.
